title: Bug: encode_rdcsr silently ignores extra operands (rdcycle/rdtime/rdinstret)
body:
# Bug: encode_rdcsr silently ignores extra operands (rdcycle/rdtime/rdinstret)
**Law:** ∀ rd ∈ GPR, ∀ extra. encode_rdcsr("rdcycle", [Reg(rd), extra]) is Err
**Impact:** `rdcycle a0, a1` (typo'd second operand) assembles silently as `csrrs a0, cycle, x0` (0xC00822F3 family) — the extra register is dropped without diagnostic. Same path for rdtime (0xC01) / rdinstret (0xC02).
**Function:** encode_rdcsr — src/backend/riscv/assembler/encoder/pseudo.rs (own operand handling, not dispatched through encode_csrr)
**Detected by:** Negative/Error Contract — extra operand (round-48 final audit `p_rdcsr_extra`, the last unclassified encode function)
**Minimal input:** encode_rdcsr("rdcycle", [Reg("a0"), Reg("a1")])
**Expected:** Err (llvm-mc: "invalid operand for instruction")
**Actual:** Ok(Word(3221235059 = 0xC00822F3 = csrrs a0, cycle, x0)) — identical to the 1-operand form

## Found by
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test --lib -- "p_rdcsr_extra" --nocapture
```

title: Bug: enums with values beyond int are silently TRUNCATED to 4 bytes — enum { X = 0x100000000LL } reads as 0; gcc/clang widen the underlying type to 8
body:
# Bug: enums with values beyond int are silently TRUNCATED to 4 bytes — enum { X = 0x100000000LL } reads as 0; gcc/clang widen the underlying type to 8
**Law:** ∀ enumerator whose value does not fit in int: the implementation must give the enum a wider underlying type (C11 6.7.2.2p4: implementation-defined, but the VALUE must be representable; gcc/clang choose 64-bit) — the constant must equal its written value. FALSIFIED — ccc forces 4-byte enums and truncates the constant to zero.
**Impact:** Silent wrong constant — compile-time data corruption:
```
enum Wide  { W31 = 0x7FFFFFFF };      fits int — fine both
enum Wider { X33 = 0x100000000LL };   beyond int:
  gcc/clang: sizeof(enum Wider)=8, (long long)X33 = 4294967296
  ccc:       sizeof(enum Wider)=4, (long long)X33 = 0        ← truncated!
enum Neg { N1 = -1, N2 = 0x80000000 }: gcc sizeof=8; ccc=4 (value also wrong)
```
Any table/flag enum using values ≥ 2^31 (common in generated protocol code) silently reads 0.
**Function:** enum constant evaluation + underlying type selection (sema enum handling) — values are stored in a 32-bit field regardless of the initializer's type.
**Detected by:** round-48 fresh-mine battery (enum underlying-type selection).
**Minimal input:** `enum E { A = 0x100000000LL }; _Static_assert-compatible check: (long long)A == 4294967296` — ccc gives 0.
**Expected:** widened underlying type, full value (gcc/clang row).
**Actual:** 4-byte enum, truncated constant.

## Found by
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
printf '#include <stdio.h>\nenum W { X = 0x100000000LL };\nint main(void){ printf("%%zu %%lld\\n", sizeof(enum W), (long long)X); }' > /tmp/e.c
gcc -w /tmp/e.c -o /tmp/g && /tmp/g   # 8 4294967296
./target/debug/ccc /tmp/e.c -o /tmp/c && /tmp/c  # 4 0
```

title: Bug: digraphs are unsupported — %:include / <% %> / <: :> rejected (C95 standard spellings; gcc/clang accept)
body:
# Bug: digraphs are unsupported — %:include / <% %> / <: :> rejected (C95 standard spellings; gcc/clang accept)
**Law:** ∀ token with a digraph spelling (`%:`=#, `<%`/`%>`=braces, `<:`/`:>`=brackets, `%:%:`=##): the digraph is equivalent to the primary spelling (C95/C99 §6.4.6 "Alternative representations"). FALSIFIED — ccc rejects them at the first token.
**Impact:**
```
%:include <stdio.h>
int main(void) <%
    int arr<:3:> = {1, 2, 3};
    printf("%d\n", arr<:1:>);
    return 0;
%>
  gcc:   compiles, prints 2
  clang: compiles
  ccc:   error: expected declaration before '%'   (line 1, first token!)
```
Digraphs matter for ISO-646 national character sets (where #, [, { may be unavailable) and appear in portability-oriented codebases.
**Function:** lexer token scanner — no digraph equivalence table.
**Detected by:** round-46 "one more sweep" batch (user-prompted final pass).
**Minimal input:** `%:include <stdio.h>` alone.
**Expected:** preprocessed as `#include`.
**Actual:** lexical error at '%'.

## Found by
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
printf '%%:include <stdio.h>\nint main(void) <%% int a<:1:> = {2}; printf("%%d\\n", a<:0:>); return 0; %%>\n' > /tmp/d.c
gcc -w /tmp/d.c -o /tmp/g && /tmp/g   # 2
./target/debug/ccc /tmp/d.c -o /tmp/c # error before '%'
```

title: Bug: duplicate STRONG symbols link silently — gcc errors 'multiple definition'; ccc resolves with an internal heuristic (order-independent pick observed)
body:
# Bug: duplicate STRONG symbols link silently — gcc errors 'multiple definition'; ccc resolves with an internal heuristic (order-independent pick observed)
**Law:** ∀ two objects defining the same GLOBAL STRONG symbol (data or function): the link must fail with a multiple-definition diagnostic (System V ABI / GNU ld behavior; ODR enforcement at link time). FALSIFIED — ccc links silently.
**Impact:** Silent ODR violations across translation units:
```
$ cat a.c: int shared = 1; int main(void){return shared;}
$ cat b.c: int shared = 2; int other(void){return shared;}
$ gcc a.c b.c -o g   → error: multiple definition of 'shared'
$ ccc  a.c b.c -o c  → links, runs, exits 1 (first TU's value)
```
Function form likewise: duplicate `int f(void)` definitions link silently in BOTH file orders (ccc returned 11 either way — some internal pick, not even first-on-command-line). Data-form duplicate picks the first TU. gcc rejects all forms.
**Function:** linker symbol resolution (src/backend/linker_common/symbols.rs) — strong/strong conflicts neither error nor warn.
**Weak/strong and tentative merges are CORRECT** (round-33 PBT + this round's order-reversal matrix: strong always wins, both orders match gcc) — only the strong/strong error path is missing.
**Detected by:** round-46 linker symbol-semantics battery.
**Minimal input:** the two files above.
**Expected:** "multiple definition of 'shared'" (gcc).
**Actual:** silent link + run.

## Found by
```bash
cd /tmp/lk
printf 'int shared = 1;\nint main(void){return shared;}' > a.c
printf 'int shared = 2;\nint other(void){return shared;}' > b.c
gcc -w a.c b.c -o g   # error
/home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler/target/debug/ccc a.c b.c -o c && ./c; echo $?
```

title: Bug: -Wl,-Map,file is silently ignored — no link map emitted (gcc/ld writes it)

# Bug: -Wl,-Map,file is silently ignored — no link map emitted (gcc/ld writes it)
**Law:** -Wl,-Map,FILE passes -Map FILE to the linker, which writes a link map (symbol/layout dump) to FILE (GCC -Wl §3.15; every real linker implements -Map). FALSIFIED — ccc produces no file and no diagnostic.
**Impact:** Build-introspection workflows (size audits, symbol placement debugging) silently get nothing:
```
$ gcc m.c -Wl,-Map,gcc.map -o a   → gcc.map written
$ ccc  m.c -Wl,-Map,ccc.map -o a  → no ccc.map, exit 0
```
(The -Wl passthrough ITSELF works for -rpath etc. — verified green; the internal linker just has no -Map support.)
**Function:** internal linker option handling (src/backend/linker_common/args.rs) — -Map accepted, no emitter.
**Detected by:** round-45 driver battery batch 5.
**Minimal input:** `ccc t.c -Wl,-Map,m.map -o t` — m.map absent.
**Expected:** map file.
**Actual:** nothing; silent no-op.

## Found by
```bash
cd /tmp/drv
gcc -w m.c -Wl,-Map,g.map -o g && ls g.map
/home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler/target/debug/ccc m.c -Wl,-Map,c.map -o c; ls c.map || echo NONE
```

**Law:** CPATH and C_INCLUDE_PATH add directories to the include search path (GCC manual §3.10/§12: "CPATH ... specifies a list of directories to be searched as if specified with -I"). FALSIFIED — ccc ignores both.

```
$ CPATH=/tmp/envinc gcc ev.c -o e && ./e    → 5      (evh.h found)
$ CPATH=/tmp/envinc ccc  ev.c -o e          → error: evh.h: No such file or directory
$ C_INCLUDE_PATH same result (gcc ok / ccc error)
```
**Function:** include-path assembly (src/driver / preprocessor includes.rs) — environment variables never consulted.
**Detected by:** round-45 driver battery batch 3.
**Minimal input:** any #include of a header reachable only via CPATH.
**Expected:** found (gcc row).

**Function:** -M generation (driver/preprocessor include tracking) — the include collector is not wired into the -M writer.

title: Bug: self-including header builds SILENTLY — #include recursion terminated without diagnostic while gcc errors '#include nested too deeply'

# Bug: self-including header builds SILENTLY — #include recursion terminated without diagnostic while gcc errors '#include nested too deeply'
**Law:** ∀ self-recursive include chain: the implementation has an include-depth LIMIT and must report exceeding it (gcc: "#include nested too deeply" at depth 200). FALSIFIED — ccc terminates the recursion somewhere silently and EMITS AN OBJECT FILE as if the source were well-formed.
**Impact:**
```
$ printf '#include "deep.h"\n' > deep.h    (self-include)
$ printf '#include "deep.h"\n#include <stdio.h>\nint main(void){return 0;}\n' > t.c
$ gcc t.c -c -o t.o    → error: #include nested too deeply
$ ccc t.c -c -o t.o    → exit 0, 640-byte .o produced silently
```
A cyclic header (typical guard-less legacy header) yields a silently-truncated translation unit instead of an error — content depends on where the hidden limit stops, i.e., nondeterministic-looking builds.
**Function:** include depth handling (src/frontend/preprocessor/includes.rs) — a depth cutoff exists (no hang) but emits no diagnostic and reports success.
**Detected by:** round-45 include battery (self-include probe with 5s timeout: no hang, but silent success vs gcc's error).
**Minimal input:** the two files above.
**Expected:** "nested too deeply" error (gcc).
**Actual:** clean exit + object file.

```bash
printf '#include "deep.h"\n' > /tmp/deep.h
```

# Bug: function-like -D is unsupported — -D 'MAX(a,b)=((a)>(b)?(a):(b))' leaves MAX an identifier ('implicit declaration of function MAX')
**Law:** -D name=definition accepts the full macro definition grammar including FUNCTION-LIKE definitions with a parameter list (GCC manual §3.9; universally used by build systems for MAX/MIN/assert shims). FALSIFIED — ccc only parses object-like -D.
**Impact:**
```
$ ccc -D 'MAX(a,b)=((a)>(b)?(a):(b))' t.c   (t.c uses MAX(3,4))
  warning: implicit declaration of function 'MAX'   ← never defined!
  no binary produced
$ gcc same flags → prints 4
```
Even the trivial body `-D 'MAX(a,b)=42'` fails the same way — the (params) form of the definition string is rejected/mis-parsed wholesale.
**Function:** CLI -D parsing (src/driver) — definition text is passed as an object-like body only; the '(' after the name (function-like form) is not recognized.
**Detected by:** round-45 driver-flags battery.
**Minimal input:** `ccc -D 'F(x)=1' t.c` where t.c uses F(2).
**Expected:** F usable as a macro (gcc).
**Actual:** implicit-declaration warning; build fails.

## Found by
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
```

title: Bug: command-line -U does not cancel a preceding -D — 'ccc -D X -U X' leaves X defined (gcc undefines; #ifdef X wrongly true)
body:
# Bug: command-line -U does not cancel a preceding -D — 'ccc -D X -U X' leaves X defined (gcc undefines; #ifdef X wrongly true)
**Law:** command-line predefined macros apply in order; a trailing -U NAME must undefine NAME even when a -D NAME precedes it (GCC manual §3.9 -U: "cancel any previous -D"). FALSIFIED — ccc keeps the macro defined.
**Impact:** Build-system conditionals misfire:
```
$ printf '#include <stdio.h>\nint main(void){ #ifdef X printf("BAD\n"); #else printf("ok\n"); #endif }' > t.c
$ gcc -D X -U X t.c && ./a.out     → ok: undefined
$ ccc  -D X -U X t.c -o t && ./t   → BAD: X still defined
```
`-E -dM` evidence: gcc emits 0 `#define X`, ccc emits 1.
**Function:** driver CLI macro handling (src/driver) — the -U list is not applied after -D when constructing the predefined-macro set.
**Detected by:** round-45 driver-flags battery.
**Minimal input:** `ccc -E -dM -D X -U X any.c | grep '#define X'` → 1 (expected 0).
**Expected:** X undefined (gcc row).
**Actual:** X defined; #ifdef X true.

## Found by
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
printf '#include <stdio.h>\nint main(void){#ifdef X printf("BAD\n"); #else printf("ok\n"); #endif}' > /tmp/u.c
gcc -w -D X -U X /tmp/u.c -o /tmp/g && /tmp/g    # ok
./target/debug/ccc -D X -U X /tmp/u.c -o /tmp/c && /tmp/c  # BAD
```

title: Bug: empty hex escapes accepted — "\x" and "\xg" compile clean; gcc errors (C11 6.4.4.4: hex-escape requires ≥1 hex digit)
body:
# Bug: empty hex escapes accepted — "\x" and "\xg" compile clean; gcc errors (C11 6.4.4.4: hex-escape requires ≥1 hex digit)
**Law:** ∀ hex escape: at least one hexadecimal digit must follow \x (C11 6.4.4.4p3 simple-escape/hex-escape grammar: hexadecimal-escape = \x hexadecimal-digit+). FALSIFIED — ccc accepts zero-digit forms.
**Impact:** gcc errors " \x used with no following hex digits"; clang errors; ccc compiles clean and the escape silently yields NUL ('\0'-like) — a typo'd escape becomes a string terminator:
```
"\x"   gcc: error; ccc: compiles, [0] == 0    ← silent string truncation
"\xg"  gcc: error; ccc: compiles, [0] == 0
```
Warning-level neighbors correctly diverge-free: "\8" and "\7777" are warnings in gcc (accepted by both).
**Function:** lexer escape scanner (src/frontend/lexer) — the \x loop tolerates zero hex digits.
**Detected by:** round-45 escape-corner battery (python-precise form isolation after shell-quoting noise).
**Minimal input:** `int main(void){ return "\x"[0]; }`
**Expected:** " \x used with no following hex digits" diagnostic.
**Actual:** clean compile, value 0.

## Found by
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
printf 'int main(void){ return "\\x"[0]; }' > /tmp/e.c
gcc -w -c /tmp/e.c -o /dev/null  # error
./target/debug/ccc /tmp/e.c -c -o /tmp/e.o && echo ACCEPTED
```

title: Bug: string literals containing RAW NEWLINES are accepted — gcc/clang reject (C11 6.4.5: newline not in the grammar of string-literal)
body:
# Bug: string literals containing RAW NEWLINES are accepted — gcc/clang reject (C11 6.4.5: newline not in the grammar of string-literal)
**Law:** ∀ string literal: its characters are s-char-sequence members which exclude the raw new-line character (C11 6.4.5p1 — new-line may not appear; the escape \\n exists for that). FALSIFIED — ccc lexes a literal containing an embedded LF and builds the object.
**Impact:** gcc errors "missing terminating \" character"; clang reports 4 errors; ccc compiles clean:
```
$ printf 'int main(void){ const char *s = "line1\nline2"; return s[5]; }' > t.c   (real newline)
  gcc:   error: missing terminating " character
  clang: error: missing terminating " ... (4 errors)
  ccc:   exit 0, object produced — the literal spans two source lines
```
Accepting raw newlines silently changes line-continuation semantics and error recovery (a stray opening quote swallows following lines in ccc while references stop at line end).
**Function:** lexer string-literal scanner (src/frontend/lexer) — no new-line termination check inside the s-char loop.
**Detected by:** round-44 giant-switch generator accident (generator emitted an invalid literal; gcc refused, ccc compiled AND RAN it — output "big=237708" from the broken source), then minimized above.
**Minimal input:** the one-liner above.
**Expected:** "missing terminating" diagnostic.
**Actual:** clean compile.

title: Bug: #if operand-type constraints absent — floating literals (1.0/1e5), strings, CASTS (forbidden by C11 6.10.1p4), invalid pp-number (0x1e+2) all accepted (5 forms)
body:
# Bug: #if operand-type constraints absent — floating literals (1.0/1e5), strings, CASTS (forbidden by C11 6.10.1p4), invalid pp-number (0x1e+2) all accepted (5 forms)
**Law:** ∀ #if controlling expression: it must be an INTEGER constant expression (C11 6.10.1p4) — floating constants, string literals, and CAST OPERATORS are all excluded ("the expression that controls conditional inclusion ... casts shall not be used"); a pp-number like `0x1e+2` is not a valid preprocessing token sequence. FALSIFIED — all 5 forms preprocess clean in ccc.
**Impact:** gcc rejects every form; ccc silently evaluates:
```
#if 0x1e+2      gcc: "exponent has no digits"/invalid pp-number
#if 1.0         gcc: "floating constant in preprocessor expression"
#if 1e5         gcc: same
#if "x"         gcc: "token "x" is not valid in preprocessor expressions"
#if (int)'A'    gcc: "casts are not allowed in preprocessor expressions" (6.10.1p4)
```
ccc accepts all — e.g. `#if (int)'A'` evaluates true, letting non-conforming conditionals silently gate code (compat trap when moving between compilers).
**Function:** expr_eval operand-type filtering (src/frontend/preprocessor) — accepts float/string/cast nodes that the #if grammar excludes. Same subsystem as #1088 (malformed-syntax acceptance) but the operand-TYPE axis.
**Detected by:** round-43 pp battery (5-form probe).
**Minimal input:** `#if 1.0\nT\n#endif` — ccc preprocesses; gcc errors.
**Expected:** the five gcc diagnostics.
**Actual:** clean preprocess for all 5.

```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
```

title: Bug: __attribute__((constructor(N))) priorities are IGNORED — ctors run in declaration order instead of ascending priority (gcc: 2→101→default)
body:
# Bug: __attribute__((constructor(N))) priorities are IGNORED — ctors run in declaration order instead of ascending priority (gcc: 2→101→default)
**Law:** ∀ pair of constructors with priorities p1 < p2: the p1 constructor runs before p2; unprioritized constructors run at default priority 65535, i.e., after all prioritized ones (GCC manual §6.39 Attribute Syntax / Common Function Attributes; implemented via .init_array priority sections `.init_array.NNNN`). FALSIFIED — ccc runs them in DECLARATION order.
**Impact:** Silent wrong initialization order for any dependency-chained static init:
```c
static int order = 0;
__attribute__((constructor))      static void c1(void) { printf("ctor1 o=%d\n", order++); }
__attribute__((constructor(101))) static void c2(void) { printf("ctor101 o=%d\n", order++); }
__attribute__((constructor(2)))   static void c3(void) { printf("ctor2 o=%d\n", order++); }
int main(void){ ... }
  gcc: ctor2(0) ctor101(1) ctor1(2) main(3)     ← priorities honored (2 < 101 < default)
  ccc: ctor1(0) ctor101(1) ctor2(2) main(3)     ← declaration order, priorities ignored
```
A dependency chain (e.g., priority 1 registering a table that priority 100 fills) silently runs backwards.
**Function:** constructor priority handling — the attribute parser accepts the (N) argument but the .init_array emission drops it (no `.init_array.NNNN` sectioning; plain FIFO .init_array).
**Detected by:** round-43 attribute semantics battery.
**Minimal input:** two prioritized ctors printing — order swaps vs gcc.
**Expected:** ascending priority order (gcc row).
**Actual:** declaration order.

## Found by
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
# /tmp/cd.c contains the witness above
gcc -w /tmp/cd.c -o g && ./g
./target/debug/ccc /tmp/cd.c -o c && ./c
```

title: Bug: asm symbol-rename labels break the link — int f(void) asm("other"); emits the call under the new name but the definition under the old (undefined symbol)
body:
# Bug: asm symbol-rename labels break the link — int f(void) asm("other"); emits the call under the new name but the definition under the old (undefined symbol)
**Law:** ∀ function declared with an asm label `T f() asm("N")`: ALL references — the emitted definition symbol AND every call site — must use N (GCC manual §6.44 "Using Assembly Labels with C Symbols"). FALSIFIED — ccc splits the two sides and fails to link.
**Impact:** A documented GNU extension used in real code (libc ABI shims, symbol versioning, name-collision avoidance) cannot link:
```c
int real_name(int x) asm("my_renamed_fn");
int real_name(int x) { return x * 3; }
int main(void) { printf("%d\n", real_name(5)); }
  gcc: compiles, links, prints 15
  ccc: ccc: error: undefined symbols: my_renamed_fn
```
ccc emits calls to my_renamed_fn but the definition keeps real_name (or vice versa) — the two halves never meet.
**Function:** asm-label handling in the symbol emitter (frontend/sema declaration → backend symbol name); only one side of the rename is applied.
**Detected by:** round-42 GNU-extension semantics dive (asm-labels probe).
**Minimal input:** the 3-line program above.
**Expected:** links (definition emitted AS my_renamed_fn).
**Actual:** "undefined symbols: my_renamed_fn".

## Found by

title: Bug: nested function support is exactly INVERTED vs gcc — plain nested fns rejected (gcc accepts as GNU extension with static links), static nested fns accepted (gcc rejects)
body:
# Bug: nested function support is exactly INVERTED vs gcc — plain nested fns rejected (gcc accepts as GNU extension with static links), static nested fns accepted (gcc rejects)
**Law:** Nested function definitions are a GNU extension implemented by gcc/clang with full semantics (parameter lists, mid-block placement, access to enclosing locals via static chain, address-escape via trampolines). A compiler either supports the extension fully or rejects it consistently. FALSIFIED — ccc's support is the exact inverse of both references:
```
form                                     gcc      clang    ccc
int main(void){ int inner(void){...} }   accept   accept   REJECT ("expected ';' before '{'")
int main(void){ int inner(int x){...} }  accept   accept   REJECT
int main(void){ static int inner(...)}   REJECT   REJECT   accept (#1150)
outer(int b){ int inner(int x){ return x+b; } ... }   accept(110)   REJECT
```
Impact: (a) code using gcc's documented nested-function extension fails to build; (b) the static variant that both references forbid compiles (#1150). The two faces need swapping/aligning.
**Function:** parser/sema nested-declarator handling — plain nested definitions hit "expected ';' after declaration before '{'" at the body brace (declarator parsed as prototype, body rejected); the static variant slips through the same path.
**Separate from #1150** (that documents the static-form acceptance alone; this issue adds the plain-form rejection — together they describe the inversion).
**Detected by:** round-42 GNU-extension semantics dive (capture/trampoline probes; gcc computes 110 with static-link semantics, ccc cannot compile).
**Minimal input:** `int main(void){ int inner(int x){ return x; } return inner(1); }`
**Expected:** accept with static-link semantics (extension) — or reject BOTH forms consistently.
**Actual:** plain rejected / static accepted.

## Found by
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
printf 'int main(void){ int inner(int x){ return x; } return inner(1); }' > /tmp/n.c
gcc -w /tmp/n.c -o /tmp/g && echo OK     # accepts (extension)
./target/debug/ccc /tmp/n.c -c -o /tmp/c.o  # error: expected ';' ... before '{'
```

title: Bug: block-scope static function definition accepted — gcc: 'invalid storage class for function', clang: 'function definition is not allowed here'

# Bug: block-scope static function definition accepted — gcc: 'invalid storage class for function', clang: 'function definition is not allowed here'
**Law:** ∀ function definition D nested in a block: D shall not have static storage class (C11 6.7.1p7 storage-class specifiers on block-scope functions are limited to (nothing/extern); nested function definitions themselves are a GNU extension but never with static). FALSIFIED — ccc compiles it.
**Impact:** gcc AND clang both reject:
```
int main(void){ static int inner(void){ return 1; } return inner(); }
  gcc:   error: invalid storage class for function 'inner'
  clang: error: function definition is not allowed here
  ccc:   compiles clean (exit 0, object produced)
```
Internal-linkage semantics for a nested definition are ill-defined; silently accepting diverges from both references.
**Function:** block-scope declarator storage-class validation (sema) — sibling of the plain nested-definition form (which gcc accepts as an extension, verified round-41 wave-8: no divergence there; the STATIC variant is the divergence).
**Detected by:** round-42 memory-graph fuzzer bring-up (gcc rejected generated programs containing block-scope static fn definitions while ccc compiled them — the 1024-reject case), confirmed minimal above.
**Minimal input:** the one-liner above.
**Expected:** the two reference diagnostics.
**Actual:** clean compile.

```
enum E; enum E e;             gcc: "variable ‘e’ has initializer but incomplete type"/"use of enum ‘E’ without previous declaration-complete"
```

title: Bug: typedef to a VLA type crashes the compiled binary — `typedef int VA[n]; VA v; v[i]=..;` SEGFAULTs (gcc runs fine); sizeof also wrong (4 vs 20)
body:
# Bug: typedef to a VLA type crashes the compiled binary — `typedef int VA[n]; VA v; v[i]=..;` SEGFAULTs (gcc runs fine); sizeof also wrong (4 vs 20)
**Law:** ∀ typedef T to a variably-modified array type of runtime length n, and object v of type T: v is a VLA of n elements — sizeof(v)=n*sizeof(elem), storage is runtime-allocated (C11 6.7.7: a typedef name "may be redefined... variably modified types" keep their runtime size). FALSIFIED — the compiled binary SEGFAULTS.
**Impact:** Crash + wrong semantics:
```c
int n = 5;
typedef int VA[n];
VA v2;
for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) v2[i] = i * 11;
printf("%d %zu\n", v2[4], sizeof(v2));
  gcc: 44 20   (correct, exits 0)
  ccc: SEGMENTATION FAULT (exit 139); sizeof(VA) object also reports 4 (one int) even before the crash path
```
The typedef loses the variably-modified property entirely: the object is laid out as a single int (sizeof 4), so the loop writes past it — stack corruption → segfault. Direct VLA `int v2[n]` works (round-34/41 batteries green); only the typedef indirection is broken.
**Function:** typedef resolution of variably-modified types (src/frontend parser/sema typedef handling + lowering array declarators) — the runtime length n is dropped when the type travels through the typedef alias.
**Separate from #1144** (that is sizeof(VLA) constant-folding to 1024 in arithmetic on DIRECT VLAs; this is the typedef-to-VLA type itself losing its element count — different root, witness crashes).
**Detected by:** round-41 runtime corner probe (typedef-VLA form).
**Minimal input:** `int main(void){ int n=5; typedef int VA[n]; VA v; v[4]=1; return v[4]; }` — crash.
**Expected:** runs, v has 5 ints (gcc row above).
**Actual:** SIGSEGV.

## Found by
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
printf '#include <stdio.h>\nint main(void){int n=5; typedef int VA[n]; VA v2; for(int i=0;i<5;i++)v2[i]=i*11; printf("%%d %%zu\\n", v2[4], sizeof(v2));}' > /tmp/t.c
gcc -w /tmp/t.c -o /tmp/g && /tmp/g          # 44 20
./target/debug/ccc /tmp/t.c -o /tmp/c && /tmp/c  # SEGFAULT
```

title: Bug: long double programs fail to LINK on ARM64 and RISC-V — toolchain emits __addtf3/__fixtfdi/__trunctfdf2 (libgcc tf3 helpers) but ships no runtime providing them
body:
# Bug: long double programs fail to LINK on ARM64 and RISC-V — toolchain emits __addtf3/__fixtfdi/__trunctfdf2 (libgcc tf3 helpers) but ships no runtime providing them
**Law:** ∀ program P using long double arithmetic: the toolchain must produce a linkable binary for every supported target (helpers the compiler itself emits must be provided by its own runtime — the libgcc contract). FALSIFIED — ARM64 and RISC-V links fail on undefined symbols the compiler itself emitted.
**Impact:** ANY long double use breaks the build on both non-x86 targets:
```
$ printf 'int main(void){ long double a=1.0L, b=2.0L; return (int)(a+b); }' > t.c
$ ccc-arm  t.c -o t   → ccc: error: undefined symbols: __addtf3, __fixtfdi, __trunctfdf2
$ ccc-riscv t.c -o t  → ccc: error: undefined symbols: __addtf3, __fixtfdi, __trunctfdf2
(full arithmetic battery additionally needs __divtf3, __eqtf2, __lttf2, __multf3, __subtf3)
```
x86-64 only works because long double maps to x87 hardware ops (no helpers). ARM64/RISC-V long double = IEEE binary128 → compiler correctly lowers to libgcc-style soft-float calls but the link step provides no compiler-rt/libgcc equivalent — the user has no flag to make it link (no -lgcc passthrough documented).
**Function:** compiler runtime packaging — missing tf3 soft-float routines for the fp128 targets (linker_common/resolve_lib should provide or link them; gcc always links libgcc automatically).
**Detected by:** round-41 cross-target runtime battery — the long-double probe (f128 arithmetic: div/mul/add/cmp/fix/trunc) failed to link on BOTH qemu targets while matching gcc on x86-64 (=132).
**Minimal input:** `int main(void){ long double a=1.0L, b=2.0L; return (int)(a+b); }` on either target.
**Expected:** links and runs (gcc links libgcc automatically; clang ships compiler-rt f128 builtins).
**Actual:** "undefined symbols: __addtf3, __fixtfdi, __trunctfdf2".
**Fix sketch:** provide the 8 tf3 routines (add/sub/mul/div/eq/lt/fix/trunc — the compiler-rt f128 builtins) as a bundled runtime object linked by default for the fp128 targets, or emit inline soft-float sequences.

## Found by
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
printf 'int main(void){ long double a=1.0L, b=2.0L; return (int)(a+b); }' > /tmp/l.c
./target/debug/ccc-arm /tmp/l.c -o /tmp/a    # undefined __addtf3...
./target/debug/ccc-riscv /tmp/l.c -o /tmp/r  # same
```

title: Bug: sizeof(VLA) constant-folds to 1024 bytes in ANY arithmetic — sizeof(v)/sizeof(v[0]) yields 256 for every VLA (the canonical array-length idiom); bare sizeof(v) is correct
body:
# Bug: sizeof(VLA) constant-folds to 1024 bytes in ANY arithmetic — sizeof(v)/sizeof(v[0]) yields 256 for every VLA (the canonical array-length idiom); bare sizeof(v) is correct
**Law:** ∀ VLA v of runtime length n and element type T: sizeof(v) is a RUNTIME value n*sizeof(T) (C11 6.5.3.4p2 — "If the type of the operand is a variable length array type, the operand is evaluated"), and every expression containing it must use that runtime value. FALSIFIED — any arithmetic operand context folds it to the constant 1024.
**Impact:** The canonical array-length idiom breaks on every VLA:
```c
int n = 7;
int v[n];
size_t s1 = sizeof(v);            // 28   ✓ (bare use correct)
size_t s2 = sizeof(v)/sizeof(int);// 256  ✗ (= 1024/4 — folded constant!)
size_t s3 = sizeof(v) * 2;        // 2048 ✗ (= 1024*2)
size_t s4 = sizeof(v) + 1;        // 1025 ✗
size_t s5 = sizeof(v) / 2;        // 512  ✗
size_t s6 = sizeof(v) >> 1;       // 512  ✗
// gcc: 28 7 56 29 14 14 — all correct
```
Any loop `for (i = 0; i < sizeof(v)/sizeof(v[0]); i++)` over a VLA iterates 256 times (or fewer for huge n) — buffer over-read/over-write with the classic idiom.
**Root cause:** the sizeof lowering emits the runtime load only in direct-use contexts; binop/constant-fold paths substitute a compile-time constant 1024 (= 256×int slot) for the VLA size instead of the runtime-computed value.
**Function:** VLA sizeof in expression folding (src/ir/lowering expr_sizeof.rs / constant_fold interplay).

title: Bug: RISC-V: FP-bearing struct returns ({float}/{double}/{float,float}) delivered in integer a0 — RV64gc psABI requires fa0(/fa1); {float,float} also DROPS the second member
body:
# Bug: RISC-V: FP-bearing struct returns ({float}/{double}/{float,float}) delivered in integer a0 — RV64gc psABI requires fa0(/fa1); {float,float} also DROPS the second member
**Law:** ∀ struct whose members are all floating-point (RV64gc psABI §18.3): returns are delivered one FP member per register in fa0, fa1. FALSIFIED — ccc-riscv moves only the first member's BITS into integer a0; {float,float} loses member b entirely.
**Impact:** Any FP-struct return crossing compilation units breaks:
```
mkf (returns {float})   : ld t0,-24(s0); mv s1,t0; mv a0,t0; ret   ← a0 integer, fa0 never loaded
mkd (returns {double})  : mv a0, t0                                ← same
mk2 (returns {f,f})     : sw t0,-24/-20(s0); ld t0,-24(s0); mv a0,t0 ← only a's bits; b stays in memory
```
Args are CORRECT (take prologue reads `fsw fa0/-24; fsw fa1/-20` — verified), so pure-ccc programs self-consistent but the return convention deviates; clang/qemu interop witness (freestanding ecall exit-code, /tmp/rv_m.c) shows all three return shapes BAD (code stayed at base).
**Function:** RISC-V FP-struct return path (call_abi classification → riscv codegen epilogue); ARG side already correct.
**Detected by:** Differential — round-38 high-value battery RISC-V extension: disassembly + clang-21 --target=riscv64-linux-gnu -march=rv64gc interop witness under qemu-riscv64-static
**Minimal input:**
```c
struct SF { float v; };
struct SF mkf(void) { struct SF s = { 2.5f }; return s; }
```
**Expected:** `fmv.w.x fa0, t0` (or flw fa0) at return; {f,f} → fa0 AND fa1.
**Actual:** `mv a0, t0` — integer register only; fa0 untouched; {f,f} drops b.
**Fix sketch:** in the RISC-V return classification, mark all-FP aggregates as FP-class (mirroring the already-correct ARGUMENT path that uses fa0/fa1) and emit per-member fmv.w.x/fmv.d.x into fa0/fa1.

title: Bug: ARM64: FP-bearing small structs ({float}/{float,float}/{double}) passed AND returned in X0/W0 integer registers — AAPCS64 HFA rule requires S/V registers; clang interop reads garbage in all 5 directions
body:
# Bug: ARM64: FP-bearing small structs ({float}/{float,float}/{double}) passed AND returned in X0/W0 integer registers — AAPCS64 HFA rule requires S/V registers; clang interop reads garbage in all 5 directions
**Law:** ∀ HFA (Homogeneous Floating-point Aggregate, AAPCS64 §6.4.2 — 1-4 FP members, ≤16B): arguments are passed in S/D/V registers and returns delivered in S0/D0/V0. FALSIFIED — ccc-arm uses integer registers (X0/W0 family) for BOTH args and returns; every direction breaks against clang.
**Impact:** Execution-verified interop (clang-21 --target=aarch64-linux-gnu caller + ccc-arm callee, qemu-aarch64-static, exit-code protocol):
```
{float}    arg → BAD      {f,f} ret → BAD
{f,f}      arg → BAD      {d}  ret → BAD
{double}   arg → BAD
(pure-clang control: all OK)
```
Disassembly witnesses (ccc-arm):
- take(struct SF {float v; }) prologue: `str x0, [sp,#16]; ldr w0, [sp,#16]` — arg from W0 (should be S0)
- mk returning {float}: `str w0,[sp,#16]; ldr x0,[sp,#16]` — return via X0 (should be S0)
- RISC-V backend is CORRECT for the same shapes (take reads fa0/fa1 — verified) — defect is ARM-backend-specific.
**Function:** ARM64 call-ABI struct classification — no HFA branch (src/backend/call_abi.rs classifier + ARM codegen param/return paths)
**Detected by:** Differential — round-38 high-value battery ARM extension: freestanding clang interop witness /tmp/arm_m3.c (bit-coded exit, 5 directions), qemu-aarch64-static
**Minimal input:**
```c
struct SF { float v; };
unsigned long long take(struct SF s) { return s.v == 2.5f ? 0xDEADULL : 0xBADULL; }
```
**Expected:** arg in S0 (`fmov s0`-path / `ldr w..` off FP save), AAPCS64 HFA.
**Actual:** arg read from W0 (`str x0,[sp,#16]`); bits happen to interop only when caller ALSO uses integer regs (pure-ccc self-consistent).
**Fix sketch:** classify HFAs in the shared classifier (all-FP members ≤4, size ≤16 → FP class), route ARM64 params/returns through s0-s7/v0-v7 mirroring the RISC-V fa-register handling already present.

title: Bug: x86-64: {long double} struct (X87 class) returned in RAX:RDX and passed in RDI:RSI — SysV requires st(0) return / memory passing; gcc interop reads -nan
body:
# Bug: x86-64: {long double} struct (X87 class) returned in RAX:RDX and passed in RDI:RSI — SysV requires st(0) return / memory passing; gcc interop reads -nan
**Law:** ∀ struct S whose eightbytes classify X87+X87UP (SysV AMD64 §3.2.3, e.g. `{ long double v; }`): a return of S must be delivered in x87 st(0), and S as an argument must be passed in MEMORY. FALSIFIED — ccc returns it in RAX:RDX (integer pair) and receives it in RDI:RSI.
**Impact:** Both directions break against gcc-compiled code:
```
$ gcc caller.c ccc_callee.o      # struct LD { long double v; }; mk returns {2.5L}
ld take=bad v=-nan                ← gcc reads st(0) (never loaded) → garbage
```
ccc mk epilogue: `popq %rax; popq %rdx; orq %rcx,%rax; orq %rsi,%rdx; ret` — x87 stack never touched.
gcc mk: `fldt LC0; fstpt -16(%rbp); fldt -16(%rbp); ret` — value in st(0).
ccc take prologue: `movq %rdi,-16(%rbp); movq %rsi,-8(%rbp)` — reads the ARG as an integer pair instead of off the stack.
**Verified-adjacent (not affected):** long double RUNTIME arithmetic is exact vs gcc (mul/div/cmp/(long long) roundtrip); >16B MEMORY-class structs (5×double) interop take=dead ✓; {double,double} SSE-pair ✓ (#1114 covers only the ≤8B single-SSE case).
**Function:** struct classification for return/args — X87/X87UP class missing from the x86-64 call-ABI handling (src/backend/call_abi.rs classify_sysv_struct family + x86 codegen return path)
**Detected by:** Differential — round-38 high-value battery manual probes (/tmp/x87_c.c + /tmp/x87_m.c), extending p_struct_interop (which caught #1114)
**Minimal input:**
```c
struct LD { long double v; };
struct LD mk(void) { struct LD s = { 2.5L }; return s; }
```

title: Bug: volatile LOCALS are constant-folded away at -O2 — `volatile int x=0; x=x+1; x=x+2;` keeps only the final store (C11 5.1.2.3 side-effect violation)
body:
# Bug: volatile LOCALS are constant-folded away at -O2 — `volatile int x=0; x=x+1; x=x+2;` keeps only the final store (C11 5.1.2.3 side-effect violation)
**Law:** ∀ object declared volatile, every read and write in the abstract machine is a side effect that must be preserved (C11 5.1.2.3p2, 6.7.3p8 "accesses to volatile objects are evaluated strictly according to the rules of the abstract machine"). FALSIFIED — all but the last store of a volatile local are eliminated and the reads constant-folded.
**Impact:** Breaks the canonical signal-handler / setjmp-recovery / MMIO-proxy idiom:
```c
volatile int x = 0; x = x + 1; x = x + 2; return x;
```
```
ccc  -O2: movq $1,%rax; movq $3,%rax; movl %eax,-8(%rbp); movq $3,%rax   ← init store, 2 loads, 2 stores GONE
gcc  -O2: movl $0,-4(%rsp); movl -4(%rsp),%eax; add $1; movl → ; movl ← ; add $2; movl → ; movl ←   ← all 6 accesses kept
```
Pointer-based volatile (`*vp` through `volatile int*`) is CORRECT — all dereferences survive (verified f1-f5 battery). Only non-address-taken volatile LOCALS are folded (storage promoted to a constant).
**Function:** constant folding / storage classification of volatile locals — optimizer treats a volatile local's storage as non-observable and propagates its initializer (src/passes, round-38 f6 witness)
**Detected by:** Differential — volatile access-preservation battery (round 38, /tmp/vol2.c f6; gcc -O2 vs ccc -O2 -S instruction comparison; DB had zero "volatile" coverage)
**Minimal input:** `int f(void) { volatile int x = 0; x = x + 1; return x; }` — must emit ≥2 loads + 2 stores; ccc emits only `movl $1`-style constants.
**Expected:** all 6 volatile accesses in the -O2 asm (gcc behavior above).
**Actual:** single final store; reads folded (`movq $3, %rax` returns constant 3 — which is also the WRONG value semantics: a signal handler mutating x between statements would be invisible).
**Fix sketch:** mark volatile locals' slots as non-foldable in constant propagation / mem2reg promotion (skip promotion + kill constant-fold-through for volatile-qualified alloca), mirroring how the pointer-deref path already preserves accesses.

## Found by

```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
cat > /tmp/v.c <<'EOF'
int f6(void) { volatile int x = 0; x = x + 1; x = x + 2; return x; }
EOF
./target/debug/ccc -O2 -S /tmp/v.c -o /tmp/v_ccc.s && gcc -O2 -S /tmp/v.c -o /tmp/v_gcc.s
diff <(grep -cE "mov.-8|mov.-4" /tmp/v_ccc.s) <(grep -cE "mov.-8|mov.-4" /tmp/v_gcc.s)  # 1 vs 6 accesses
```

title: Bug: x86-64: small SSE-class struct returns ({float}/{double}/{float,float} ≤ 8B) left in RAX — SysV requires XMM0; gcc interop reads garbage (mk → 0.0)
body:
# Bug: x86-64: small SSE-class struct returns ({float}/{double}/{float,float} ≤ 8B) left in RAX — SysV requires XMM0; gcc interop reads garbage (mk → 0.0)
**Law:** ∀ struct S with sizeof ≤ 8 whose single eightbyte classifies SSE (SysV AMD64 §3.2.3): a function returning S must deliver it in xmm0. FALSIFIED — ccc leaves it in rax and never writes xmm0.
**Impact:** Any cross-TU/cross-library call where a gcc- (or system-) compiled caller reads a ccc-compiled function's small float-struct return reads xmm0 = garbage:
```
$ gcc caller.c ccc_compiled_callee.o   # {float v;} / {double v;} / {float,float}
{double} take=bad mk=0.000             # arg path fine; RETURN broken
{float}  take=bad mk=0.000
{float,float} take=bad mk=(0.000000,0.000000)
{double,double} take=dead mk=2.5,3.5   # 16B (len==2) path correct
```
16-byte two-eightbyte returns and mixed INTEGER+SSE cases ARE handled; arguments are received correctly (`movq %xmm0, -8(%rbp)`). Only the ≤8B single-SSE-eightbyte RETURN path deviates — pure-ccc programs self-consistent, interop breaks.
**Function:** epilogue struct-return shuffle — src/backend/x86/codegen/returns.rs:74 (`if self.func_ret_classes.len() == 2` handles all mixed/double-SSE cases; no `len() == 1 && Sse` branch exists)
**Detected by:** Differential — gcc-caller/ccc-callee interop property p_struct_interop_gcc_calls_ccc (round 38, 250 cases; shrunk to `struct { float m0; float m1; }`)
**Minimal input:**
```c
struct S { double v; };
struct S mk(void) { struct S s = { 2.5 }; return s; }
```
**Expected:** epilogue does `movq %rax, %xmm0` (gcc -O0 mk: `movq -8(%rbp), %xmm0`), value readable by gcc caller via xmm0.
**Actual:** epilogue emits only `movq -8(%rbp), %rax; movq %rax, %r10; ret` — xmm0 never written; gcc caller does `movq %xmm0, %rax` → 0.0.
**Fix sketch:** in returns.rs, add the single-eightbyte case: `if self.func_ret_classes.len() == 1 && self.func_ret_classes[0] == Sse { emit("movq %rax, %xmm0") }` (mirroring the existing len==2 shuffles).

title: Bug: encode_bltz silently ignores extra operands
body:
# Bug: encode_bltz silently ignores extra operands
**Law:** ∀ rs ∈ GPR, ∀ tgt ∈ LabelIdents, ∀ extra. encode_bltz([Reg(rs), Symbol(tgt), extra]) is Err
**Impact:** A third (or later) operand is dropped with no diagnostic, so `bltz a0, foo, a1` encodes as `blt a0, x0, foo`. Typos and extra commas assemble without error and emit a valid branch relocation.
**Function:** encode_bltz
**Detected by:** Negative/Error Contract — extra operand
**Minimal input:** encode_bltz([Reg("a0"), Symbol("foo"), Reg("a1")])
**Expected:** Err (llvm-mc: "invalid operand for instruction"; README documents `blez/bgez/...` → corresponding `bge`/`blt` with x0 — two operands)
**Actual:** Ok(WordWithReloc { word: 0x00054063, reloc: Relocation { reloc_type: Branch, symbol: "foo", addend: 0 } }) — encodes as if the extra operand were absent.
**Severity:** medium
**Regression test:** src/backend/riscv/assembler/encoder/encode_bltz_pbt.rs test_encode_bltz_regression_extra_operand

title: Bug: linker output has no .symtab/.strtab — nm reports "no symbols", gdb/perf symbolization impossible, no flag to enable
body:
# Bug: linked executables drop the static symbol table entirely

**Formal:** A default link (no -s/--strip-all) must emit .symtab/.strtab carrying the input objects' defined symbols (main, globals, functions) — matching ld/lld/gcc behavior. FALSIFIED: output contains only .dynsym (3 entries: null, printf, __libc_start_main) + .shstrtab; every defined symbol is unrepresentable.

**Impact:** Toolchain interop failure on every ccc-linked binary:
```
$ nm elf_check
nm: elf_check: no symbols

$ readelf -SW elf_check | grep -E 'symtab|strtab'
  [25] .shstrtab ...        <- only section-name table; no .symtab/.strtab

$ readelf -sW elf_check
Symbol table '.dynsym' contains 3 entries: null, printf@GLIBC, __libc_start_main@GLIBC
```
- gdb: no function names, breakpoints by name impossible
- perf/addr2line/backtrace_symbolize: unresolved addresses
- nm/objdump -t: empty
- No CLI flag exists to enable it (checked --help: no strip/symbol/debug options) — the user has NO path to a symbolized binary. Input .o files DO have correct .symtab (9 entries, nm shows main/helper/shared_val), so the loss happens in the link step.

**Root cause:** the executable writer never emits SHT_SYMTAB/SHT_STRTAB. linker_common's gc_sections.rs/merge.rs/parse_object.rs handle SHT_SYMTAB of *input* objects (symbol resolution works — multi-TU linking is byte-exact vs gcc in 200-case PBT), but the output side (executable assembly path) skips static symbol emission entirely.

**Separate from:** dedup "symtab|nm no symbols|debug symbol missing|gdb symbol" = 0 hits across ~1090 issues.

**Detected by:** round-35 elf structural health sweep (readelf -a/-s/-SW differential vs gcc binary; gcc output has 2 symbol tables with all 4 defined symbols visible).

**Minimal input:**
```bash
echo 'int main(){return 0;}' > t.c
ccc t.c -o t && nm t    # "no symbols" — expected: 0000... T main
```

**Fix sketch:** after section layout, build .symtab from all defined input symbols (resolved addresses, LOCAL/GLOBAL binding, FUNC/OBJECT types, sizes) + .strtab, mark non-ALLOC so they don't load at runtime (matches ld).

## Found by
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler

printf 'int shared_val = 42;\nint helper(int x){return x*2;}' > /tmp/m2.c
./target/debug/ccc /tmp/m1.c /tmp/m2.c -o /tmp/elf_check
readelf -sW /tmp/elf_check   # only .dynsym
nm /tmp/elf_check            # no symbols
```

title: Bug: __VA_OPT__ not implemented in macro expansion — emitted as literal tokens into the output stream
body:
# Bug: __VA_OPT__ passes through literally

**Formal:** For every variadic macro `#define M(fmt, ...) fmt __VA_OPT__(, __VA_ARGS__)`: `M(x)` must expand without the variadic tail; `M(x, 7)` must expand with it (C23 6.10.5.2 / gcc clang behavior). FALSIFIED: the literal tokens `__VA_OPT__ ( , ... )` appear in the output stream unexpanded.

**Impact:** Token-stream differential (ccc vs gcc):
```c
#define V2(fmt, ...) fmt __VA_OPT__(| __VA_ARGS__)
V2(x);        // gcc: x            ccc: x __VA_OPT__ ( | )
V2(x, 7);     // gcc: x | 7        ccc: x __VA_OPT__ ( | 7 )
```
The unexpanded `__VA_OPT__ ( ... )` reaches the C parser — syntax errors on headers that legitimately use __VA_OPT__ (glibc <sys/cdefs.h>, common logging macros). No "unsupported feature" diagnostic either: it fails downstream with a confusing parser error.

**Scope:** __VA_OPT__ is the C23 spelling (also a widespread gcc/clang extension used since C99 days for the comma problem). 18/20 other macro-expansion corners are byte-exact vs gcc (paste with empty operands, stringize with spaces, self/mutual recursion barriers, variadic empty args, nested stringize, comments, line continuations — all verified green in the same sweep), so this is the single missing expansion feature in an otherwise solid macro engine.

**Root cause:** macro body expansion path (src/frontend/preprocessor/macro_defs.rs) has no __VA_OPT__ handling — the token is treated as an ordinary identifier.

**Separate from:** dedup "VA_OPT|va_opt|VAOPT" = 0 hits across ~1085 issues.

**Detected by:** round-32 preprocessor deep PBT — `p_macro_corners_vs_gcc` (20-form token-stream differential, 18 green / 2 fail).

**Minimal input:**
```c
#define V2(fmt, ...) fmt __VA_OPT__(, __VA_ARGS__)
V2(x);   // expands to "x __VA_OPT__ ( , )" instead of "x"
```

title: Bug: #if accepts malformed expressions with no diagnostic — 8/13 silently evaluate into a branch (e.g. '#if 1 +' takes TRUE)
body:
# Bug: #if expression parser accepts invalid syntax, zero diagnostics, wrong branch

**Formal:** For every #if expression E that is not a valid integer constant expression: the preprocessor must emit a diagnostic (C11 6.10.1p4 constraint violation) and must not silently select a branch. FALSIFIED: 12/13 malformed expressions produce zero diagnostics; 8 silently select the TRUE branch.

**Impact:** A typo in a real header silently compiles the wrong variant instead of erroring:
```
expression     gcc              ccc
#if ^2         error            FALSE branch (no diagnostic)
#if 1 +        error: expected  TRUE branch   <- truncated expr silently true
#if (1         error            TRUE branch   <- unbalanced paren
#if !          error            TRUE branch
#if 1 ++ 2     error            TRUE branch
#if ~          error            TRUE branch
#if #1         error            TRUE branch
#if 1 2        error            TRUE branch   <- adjacent literals
#if x = 5      error            FALSE branch  <- assignment accepted
#if **3        error            FALSE branch
#if ??         error            FALSE branch
```
(All gcc errors are "#if with no expression"/"token is not valid in preprocessor expressions" family; ccc emits nothing and picks a branch.)

**Root cause:** expr_eval.rs evaluation path — after `replace_remaining_idents_with_zero` and `resolve_defined_in_expr`, the token-to-value parse treats unknown/truncated token sequences as 0/operand-lookup failure without a hard error; partial stacks resolve instead of failing.

**Separate from:** no existing issue mentions `#if` or `expr_eval` (dedup: 0 hits across ~1085 titles+bodies).

**Detected by:** round-32 preprocessor deep PBT — `p_if_corners_vs_gcc` skip analysis (gcc=None, ccc=Some) + manual sweep of 13 malformed forms via `ccc -E` vs `gcc -E -P`.

**Minimal input:**
```c
#if 1 +
int wrong_branch_selected;
#endif
```

**Fix sketch:** the #if expression parser needs a strict mode: any unconsumed token, unbalanced paren, dangling operator, or non-expression token must return Err → emit diagnostic (matching gcc behavior of failing the conditional rather than guessing).

title: Bug: compound literal with nested array initializer drops row elements - &(int[3][3]){...} emits only each row's first element
body:
# Bug: nested-array compound literal data corruption

**Formal:** For every compound literal `(T[n][m]){ {r0...}, {r1...}, ... }` at global scope: the emitted backing object must equal gcc's byte-for-byte (all n*m elements). FALSIFIED: only each row's FIRST element is emitted; remaining elements are zero/garbage.

**Impact:** Silent data corruption for any address-taken 2-D (or nested) array compound literal:
```c
static int (*ca)[3] = &(int[3][3]){ {1,2,3}, {4,5,6}, {7,8,9} };
static int (*cb)[2] = &(int[2][2]){ {10,20}, {30,40} };
printf("cb=%d %d %d %d\n", cb[0][0], cb[0][1], cb[1][0], cb[1][1]);
  gcc: cb=10 20 30 40
  ccc: cb=10 0 30 0        <- 20 and 40 silently dropped
printf("ca1=%d %d %d\n", ca[1][0], ca[1][1], ca[1][2]);
  gcc: ca1=4 5 6
  ccc: ca1=0 7 0           <- backing data = [1,0,4,0,7,0] then uninitialized
                              (ca[2][2] reads into the ADJACENT global cp -> 10)
```
Backing-data reconstruction from reads: emitted words are `[1,0,4,0,7,0]` = each row contributes exactly ONE element + one zero, then the allocation trails uninitialized memory (reads leak the next global).

**Root cause:** `create_compound_literal_global` (src/ir/lowering/global_init.rs:1142) - for `TypeSpecifier::Array(elem_ts=int[3], _)` it takes `num_elems = items.len()` (=3 rows, alloc 36 bytes correct) but the nested per-row `Initializer::List` flattening in the subsequent `lower_global_init` path emits only each row's first scalar. Regular (non-compound) 2-D global initializers `int g[4][3] = {{...}}` are byte-exact vs gcc (verified in the same round, 300-case PBT), so the defect is specific to the compound-literal path.

**Separate from:** no existing issue mentions compound literals (dedup: "compound.literal" 0 hits across all ~1080 issue titles+bodies).

**Detected by:** round-31 ir/lowering deep PBT - property `p_compound_designated_statics_vs_gcc` (global compound literals + designated init + static locals), shrunk first case.

**Minimal input:**
```c
static int (*cb)[2] = &(int[2][2]){ {10,20}, {30,40} };
// cb[0][1] reads 0 instead of 20
```

**Fix sketch:** when `is_array` and the element type is itself an array, recurse the flattening per row (each row-List must emit all m elements at elem offsets), matching the non-compound path's handling.

title: Bug: f128_bytes_to_x87_bytes truncates 49 mantissa bits — every long double literal on x86 is up to 1 ulp low (0.1L, pi misprinted)
body:
# Bug: f128_bytes_to_x87_bytes truncates instead of round-to-nearest

**Formal:** ∀ decimal long-double literal L with a non-representable binary expansion: bytes_ccc(L) == bytes_gcc(L) (both must be the correctly rounded x87-80 encoding of L). FALSIFIED: 7/8 sample literals are exactly 1 ulp LOW.

**Impact:** Every `long double` literal in a program compiled for x86/x86-64 is up to 1 ulp LOW. Observable at printf level:
```
printf("%.25Lf", 0.1L);
  gcc: 0.1000000000000000000013553
  ccc: 0.0999999999999999999945790    <- wrong from 20th digit
printf("%.25Lf", 3.14159265358979323846L);
  gcc: 3.1415926535897932385128090
  ccc:  3.1415926535897932382959685
```
Byte-level witnesses (16-byte x87 dump, first byte = mantissa LSB):
```
0.1L:                 gcc cd cc .. vs ccc cc cc ..
123456.789012345678L: gcc e4 69 .. vs ccc e3 69 ..
2.718281828459045235L: gcc 9b 4a .. vs ccc 9a 4a ..
999999.9999999999999L: gcc ..00 24 f4 vs ccc ..ff 23 f4
```

**Root cause:** `f128_bytes_to_x87_bytes` (src/common/long_double.rs:886) narrows the 113-bit f128 mantissa with `let mantissa64 = (mantissa >> 49) as u64;` — the comment says "Take top 64 bits". The dropped 49 bits need round-to-nearest-even (guard = bit 48, sticky = bits 47..0, plus mantissa-overflow renormalization). The decimal→f128 stage (round_to_nearest_even_113) is correct; only the second f128→x87 stage truncates.

**Blast radius:** consumers in src/backend/x86/codegen/calls.rs and src/backend/common.rs — x86-64 long-double data emission (`.tfloat`-equivalent) for every long double literal.

**Separate from:** #517 (f128_bytes_to_f64, line 906 — f64 narrowing, const-fold path), #516/#576 (subnormal paths in ir/constants.rs f64_to_* functions). Different function, different consumers, independent fix (add RNE to the 49-bit drop here).

**Fix sketch:** after `let mut m = mantissa >> 49;` apply `if (mantissa >> 48) & 1 == 1 && ((mantissa & ((1u128<<48)-1)) != 0 || m & 1 == 1) { m += 1; if m >> 64 != 0 { m = 1u64 << 63; biased_exp += 1; } }`.

**Detected by:** round-31 global-initializer PBT (byte-exact differential vs gcc, property p_global_init_bytes_vs_gcc, first shrunk case) — ir/lowering deep PBT campaign.

**Minimal input:**
```c
static long double a = 0.1L;
```

title: Bug: encode_shift panics on subtraction overflow when shift amount >= register width (lsl w0, w1, #32 → "attempt to subtract with overflow")
body:
# Bug: encode_shift panics on subtraction overflow
**Law:** encode_shift returns Result<EncodeResult, String> — out-of-range inputs must produce Err, never panic. For W registers, shift amount must be 0..31; 32 is out of range.
**Impact:** `encode_shift([Reg("w0"), Reg("w1"), Imm(32)], 0)` panics with "attempt to subtract with overflow" in debug mode. In release mode it silently computes a huge imms value, producing a wrong instruction. The panic is at `imms = width - 1 - imm` where `width=32, imm=32` → `31 - 32` → u32 underflow.
**Function:** encode_shift (data_processing.rs, LSL immediate path)
**Source location:** src/backend/arm/assembler/encoder/data_processing.rs:811 — `let imms = width - 1 - imm;` (u32 underflow when imm >= width)
**Detected by:** round-30 adversarial encode PBT (p_shift_64_on_w)
**Minimal input:** `encode_shift([Reg("w0"), Reg("w1"), Imm(32)], 0)` → panics
**Expected:** Err("shift amount out of range") or equivalent
**Actual:** debug panic "attempt to subtract with overflow"
**Severity:** medium (crash in debug, silent wrong encoding in release)
**Contract evidence:** inferred (Result return type is the error contract)
**Fix:** Check `imm < width` before computing `imms = width - 1 - imm`, return Err for out-of-range shift. Also check LSR/ASR paths (same `width - 1` calculation without imm check).

title: Bug: AArch64 assembler encodes ALL fmov Rd, #imm (FP immediate) forms as NOP — fmov d0, #1.0 produces 1f2003d5 (NOP) instead of 00106e1e

# Bug: AArch64 fmov with floating-point immediate encodes as NOP
**Law:** FMOV (immediate) loads a floating-point constant encoded as an 8-bit immediate (imm8 encodes a limited set of FP values). Both refs produce exact encodings.
**Impact:** ALL 10 tested `fmov Rd, #float` forms encode as NOP (`1f2003d5`): fmov d0,#1.0, #2.0, #-1.0, #0.0, #0.125, d1,#3.5, s0,#1.0, #31.0, #0.0, s1,#-2.0. The FP register is NEVER SET — any code relying on fmov-immediate silently gets an unset register. The 28 non-immediate scalar FP forms (fadd/fmul/fdiv/fsqrt/fneg/fabs/fmax/fmin/fcvt/fcvtzs/scvtf/frinti/frinta) all encode correctly. The compiler's own codegen avoids this path (uses integer movq for FP constants), so E2E tests pass — the bug only affects external .s files using fmov-immediate.
**Function:** AArch64 assembler scalar FP immediate encoder
**Detected by:** round-28 scalar FP battery (38 forms; 28 OK, 2 GAP, 10 DIFF — ALL fmov-imm forms NOP)
**Minimal input:** `.text` / `fmov d0, #1.0` → ccc `1f2003d5` (NOP); mc `00106e1e` (fmov d0,#1.0)
**Severity:** HIGH (silent NOP = FP register never set; same pattern as #839 fcmp #0.0 and #1057 fcmeq #0.0)

# Bug: AArch64 NEON FP compare-vs-zero: NOP encoding + wrong encodings + missing mnemonics
**Law:** NEON FP comparisons against #0.0 have dedicated encodings (cond field selects eq/gt/le/lt). Both refs produce exact bytes.
**Impact:** Three classes (45/51 NEON shift+cmp forms byte-exact ✓):
1. **NOP encoding (2 forms):** `fcmeq v0.4s, v1.4s, #0.0` and `fcmgt v0.4s, v1.4s, #0.0` → ccc encodes `1f2003d5` = NOP! The comparison is SILENTLY SKIPPED — vectorized FP equality/ordering checks against zero produce garbage. Same symptom as scalar #839 (fcmp d0,#0.0 → NOP) but in the NEON path.
2. **Wrong encoding (2 forms):** `fcmlt v0.4s, v1.4s, #0.0` → ccc `20d8a04e` (this is fcmeq's encoding!) vs mc `20e8a04e` (correct fcmlt). `fcmle v0.4s, v1.4s, #0.0` → ccc `20d8206e` (bit 23 wrong) vs mc `20d8a06e`.
3. **Missing (2 forms):** `sqshlu` (saturating shift-left-unsigned) and `cmls` (carry-less-set comparison) — both refs accept; ccc rejects.
**Function:** AArch64 assembler NEON FP comparison path
**Detected by:** round-28 NEON shift+cmp battery (51 forms; 45 OK, 2 GAP, 4 DIFF)
**Minimal input:** `.text` / `fcmeq v0.4s, v1.4s, #0.0` → ccc encodes NOP (`1f2003d5`)

# Bug: encode_vid_v ignores trailing v0.t and hardcodes vm=1
**Law:** ∀ vd ∈ {0..31}. let mc = llvm-mc("vid.v v{vd}, v0.t"); let sut = encode_vid_v([Reg("v{vd}"), Symbol("v0.t")]). (mc = Ok(w) ⇒ sut = Ok(w)) ∧ (mc = Err ⇒ sut = Err)
**Impact:** RISC-V V 1.0 vid.v is maskable. llvm-mc `-triple=riscv64 -mattr=+v` encodes `vid.v v1, v0.t` as 0x5008a0d7 (vm=0) and rejects `vid.v v0, v0.t` (destination overlaps the mask register). **Actual:** Ok(Word(0x5208a057)) — same encoding as unmasked `vid.v v0`. Likewise encode_vid_v([Reg("v1"), Symbol("v0.t")]) = Ok(Word(0x5208a0d7)) vs llvm-mc 0x5008a0d7.

title: Bug: sema accepts _Generic with no matching type and no default — C11 requires exactly one association to match
body:
# Bug: sema accepts _Generic with no matching type and no default
**Law:** C11 6.5.1.1p2: "exactly one of the associations shall be selected" — if the selector type matches no association and there is no default, the program is ill-formed. gcc rejects with "error: _Generic selector of type int is not compatible with any association".
**Impact:** `_Generic(x, double: 1.0, char*: \str\)` with `int x` compiles silently — the result is undefined behavior. Also: ccc does not type-check non-selected branches (gcc validates ALL branches compile for the given selector type, catching bugs like `strcmp(double, double)` in the wrong branch).
**Function:** sema _Generic association matching
**Source location:** src/frontend/sema/ (no completeness check + no branch type validation)
**Detected by:** round-28 _Generic dispatch battery (20-type matrix passed except signed char #1047; this separate defect found during complex dispatch testing)

title: Bug: AArch64 FP16 arithmetic encoded as FP32 — fadd h0,h1,h2 produces fadd s0,s1,s2 bytes (wrong type field)

# Bug: AArch64 FP16 arithmetic encoded as FP32 (wrong type field)
**Law:** FP16 (h-register) arithmetic uses type=11 (half) in the FP data-processing encoding; FP32 (s-register) uses type=00. These are different instruction encodings.
**Impact:** ccc encodes `fadd h0, h1, h2` as `2028221e` = fadd **s**0,s1,s2 (type=00); correct is `2028e21e` = fadd **h**0,h1,h2 (type=11). Every FP16 arithmetic instruction silently becomes the FP32 version — completely wrong semantics. Affects 19+ instructions: fadd, fsub, fmul, fdiv, fneg, fabs, fsqrt, fmax, fmin, fmov h,w / w,h, fcvtzs/fcvtns/fcvtps/fcvtas/fcvtms h,w, scvtf/ucvtf h,w. Also fcmp/fcmpe silently accepted.
**Function:** AArch64 assembler FP arithmetic type field selection
**Detected by:** round-28 FP16 battery (31 forms; 19 BUG + 2 byte-diff on ldr/str filed separately)
**Minimal input:** `.text` / `fadd h0, h1, h2` → ccc `2028221e` (fadd s0,s1,s2); llvm-mc(+fullfp16) `2028e21e` (fadd h0,h1,h2)
**Expected:** type=11 for h registers
**Actual:** type=00 (s register encoding)
**Severity:** high (silent wrong instruction — half-precision computation silently becomes single-precision)

# Bug: sema accepts named zero-width bit-field
**Law:** C11 6.7.2.1: a zero-width bit-field must be UNNAMED (`int : 0;` forces alignment); a NAMED bit-field with width 0 is a constraint violation. gcc rejects with "error: zero width for bit-field".

title: Bug: AArch64 scalar FP: X/W register names silently accepted as FP operands (fadd/fsqrt/fmax); fcmp #0.0 encodes NOP; fnmul/fcmpe/fcsel missing
body:
# Bug: AArch64 scalar FP instruction validation and encoding defects
**Law:** FP instructions require FP register names (s/d/h); `#0.0` comparison has a dedicated encoding; fnmul/fcmpe/fcsel are standard mnemonics.
**Impact:** Four classes (21/32 byte-exact ✓ including all valid s/d arithmetic):
1. **Silent wrong-instruction (5 BUGs):** `fadd x0, x1, x2` → `2028221e` = fadd **s**0,s1,s2; `fmul w0,w1,w2` → s-form; `fdiv x0` → s; `fsqrt x0` → `20c0211e` = fsqrt s0,s1; `fmax x0` → s-form. Every GPR name in an FP slot silently encodes as the s-register with the same number.
2. **Wrong encoding (2 BYTE-DIFFs):** `fcmp d0, #0.0` → ccc encodes `1f2003d5` = **NOP** (not the fcmp-vs-zero `0820601e`); `fcmp s1, #0.0` → also NOP (`2820201e` expected). The comparison against literal zero is silently skipped.
3. **Missing mnemonics (4 GAPs):** `fnmul d0,d1,d2` / `fnmul s0,s1,s2`; `fcmpe d0,d1` / `fcmpe s0,s1` (raise-exception compare); `fcsel d0,d1,d2,eq` / `fcsel s0,s1,s2,mi` (FP conditional select) — all standard, both refs accept.
**Function:** AArch64 assembler scalar FP encoder (register-class check + #0.0 comparison path + mnemonic table)
**Detected by:** round-26v 32-form scalar FP battery (21 clean byte-exact; 5+2+4 = 11 defects)
**Minimal input:** `.text` / `fcmp d0, #0.0` → ccc-arm encodes a NOP; the comparison never happens
**Expected:** Err for GPR names; `0820601e` for fcmp d0,#0.0; Ok for fnmul/fcmpe/fcsel
**Actual:** silent s-register coercion / NOP encoding / rejection of valid mnemonics
**Severity:** high (fcmp #0.0 → NOP is a silent semantic skip; GPR-as-FP is silent wrong instruction)
**Regression test:** (to add)

**Law:** BTI requires the +bti extension; RMIF requires +mte; rev32 on W registers is a documented alias that GNU as and llvm-mc both accept. Each must be gated and encoded per its encoding rules.
**Impact:** Three classes (25/31 clean byte-exact ✓ including rbit/rev/clz/cls/rev16/pac/nop/yield/wfe/wfi/sev/sevl):

2. `rmif x0, #3, #nzcv` — silently encoded (`1f2003d5`) without +mte gate. llvm-mc needs `-mattr=+mte`.

# Bug: AArch64 register-offset load/store extension forms have wrong encodings
**Law:** In register-offset addressing `[xN, xM, ext]`, the extension specifier determines the extend-and-shift option bits. A bare `sxtw` or `uxtw` (without an explicit lsl shift) has a specific option encoding; both refs produce exact bytes. SIMD register loads (`ldr b0`) have their own option encoding.
**Impact:** Two classes found:
1. **Silent accept (7 forms):** `ldr x0, [x1, x2, sxtw]`, `ldr x0, [x1, x2, uxtw]`, `ldr x0, [x1, x2, sxtw #3]`, `ldrb w0, [x1, x2, sxtw]`, `ldrh w0, [x1, x2, sxtw #1]`, `ldrsw x0, [x1, x2, sxtw #2]`, `str x0, [x1, x2, sxtw #3]` — both refs reject; ccc accepts (encodes as `ldr x0,[x1,x2]` with option bits = 0 = lsl — silently dropping the extension).
2. **Byte mismatch (1 form):** `ldr b0, [x1, x2, lsl #0]` — ccc `206862fc`, llvm-mc `2078623c` — wrong option field (0x6 vs 0x7 = b-register load encoding).
**Function:** AArch64 assembler register-offset addressing option encoding
**Detected by:** round-26s 20-form extend battery (13 clean byte-exact ✓; 7 BUG + 1 byte-diff)
**Minimal input:** `.text` / `ldr x0, [x1, x2, sxtw]` → ccc-arm assembles `206862fc` (option=lsl, extension dropped); both refs reject
**Expected:** Err for bare sxtw/uxtw; byte `2078623c` for ldr b0
**Actual:** silently encoded with extension dropped / wrong option field
**Severity:** medium (silent wrong addressing mode — the #776 class)

# Bug: AArch64 cset/cneg silently accept the AL (always) condition
**Law:** cset/cneg encode as csinc/csneg with the INVERSE condition; the AL (always, cond=1110) condition makes the conditional-select degenerate (always-taken = just a mov/neg) and is rejected by both GNU as and llvm-mc.
**Impact:** `cset x0, al` encodes `e0f79f9a` (csinc x0, xzr, xzr, nv — the AL encoding maps to the NEVER slot in the csinc alias table, producing a constant-0 result instead of the "always set to 1" the source text implies). `cneg x0, x1, al` → `20f481da` (csneg x0, x1, x1, nv — produces x1 not -x1). Silent wrong semantics.
**Function:** AArch64 assembler condition-code validation in cset/cneg paths
**Detected by:** round-26k 85-form condition-code sweep (all 14 codes × 5 instruction families; 83 clean, AL in cset/cneg silently accepted)
**Minimal input:** `.text` / `cset x0, al` → ccc-arm assembles `e0f79f9a`; llvm-mc rejects
**Expected:** Err (cond=al in cset/cneg alias)
**Actual:** silently encoded into the nv slot — wrong runtime value
**Severity:** medium (silent wrong semantics — the encoded instruction produces the INVERSE of what the text implies)
**Regression test:** (to add)

title: Bug: AArch64 parser accepts XZR/WSP/x31 as memory base addresses (ldr/ldp/str silently encode as SP-based loads)

# Bug: AArch64 parser accepts XZR/WSP/x31 as memory base addresses
**Law:** XZR (reg 31 in non-base context) and WSP are not valid memory base addresses. `ldr x0, [xzr]` means "load from address 0" via a register that doesn't hold addresses; `str x0, [wsp]` uses the 32-bit stack pointer name in a 64-bit base slot. Both are invalid; only SP (x31 in base context) is legal.
**Impact:** `ldr x0, [xzr]` encodes `e00340f9` = ldr x0, [sp] — XZR's reg-31 number is silently treated as SP in the base slot; `str x0, [wsp]` → `e00300f9` = str x0, [sp] — the 32-bit WSP name silently becomes SP. Both as and llvm-mc reject all six forms (`[xzr]`, `[x31]`, `[wsp]` in ldr/ldp/str).
**Function:** AArch64 assembler parser (base-register validation — #825 class at the addressing path)
**Detected by:** round-26j zero-register-in-base battery (14 forms, 6 BUGs)
**Minimal input:** `.text` / `ldr x0, [xzr]` → ccc-arm assembles `e00340f9` (ldr x0, [sp])
**Expected:** Err (xzr is not a base register)
**Actual:** silently encoded as SP-based load
**Severity:** medium
**Regression test:** (to add to pbt_asm_deep)

title: Bug: x86 parser accepts every non-GPR register class in GPR slots (mm0/cs/st(0) in addq; cs in pushq) — #826's class extends to all register classes + i686 backend
body:
# Bug: x86 parser accepts every non-GPR register class in GPR operand slots
**Law:** GPR-only instructions must reject every non-GPR register name (MMX, segment, x87 stack) in integer operand slots. The numeric suffix of any register name (mm0→0, cs→1, st(0)→0) must not be silently reinterpreted.
**Impact:** `addq %mm0, %rax` encodes `4801c0` = add %rax,%rax; `addq %cs, %rax` → `4801c8` = add %rax,%rcx (cs's internal num 1); `pushq %cs` → `51` = push %rcx; `addq %st(0), %rax` → `4801c0` = add %rax,%rax. i686 same class: `addl %xmm0, %eax` → `01c0`; `pushl %xmm0` → `50` = push %eax. Both as and llvm-mc reject all six.
**Function:** x86 assembler parser (register-name → register-class binding — NO class check at all; #826 was the xmm case, this extends it to mm0/cs/st(0) + the i686 path)
**Detected by:** round-26i cross-class battery (12 forms, 6 new BUGs across x86-64 and i686)
**Minimal input:** `.text` / `addq %cs, %rax` → ccc assembles `4801c8` (add %rax,%rcx)
**Expected:** Err (register class mismatch)
**Actual:** silently encoded as the internal-number GPR
**Severity:** medium
**Regression test:** (to add to pbt_asm_deep)

title: Bug: RISC-V assembler silently accepts out-of-range immediates across 4 more instruction paths (auipc negative, jalr ±2048 boundary, csrrw csr ≥ 4096, sb 2048) — #796's class is systemic
body:
# Bug: RISC-V assembler silently accepts out-of-range immediates across 4 more instruction paths

**Law:** Each RISC-V instruction's immediate field has a fixed width and range; an out-of-range immediate is unencodable and must be rejected (the ISA field width is the contract). Round 17 (#796) filed the imm12 range on the addi/load/store path; this round's boundary battery shows the SAME missing-range-check on four MORE paths:

| Form | Valid range | ccc bytes (decodes to) |
|------|-------------|------------------------|
| `auipc a0, -1` | [0, 65535] (U-type imm20 **unsigned**) | `17f5ffff` — imm20 = 0xFFFFF (≈ 4MB offset, not -4KB) |
| `jalr a0, 2048(a1)` | [-2048, 2047] (I-type imm12) | `67850580` — imm12 bits = 0x800 (decodes as **-2048**) |
| `jalr a0, -2049(a3)` | [-2048, 2047] | silently accepted (low 12 bits = 2047) |
| `csrrw a0, 4096, a1` | [0, 4095] (12-bit CSR index) | `73950500` — CSR field = 0 (**cycle** reg, not 4096) |
| `sb a0, 2048(a1)` | [-2048, 2047] (S-type imm12) | `2380a580` — decodes as sb #2047 |

**Impact:** External `.s` files with boundary typos silently assemble to different instructions than written — e.g. `csrrw a0, 4096, a1` accesses CSR 0 (cycle) instead of erroring; `jalr a0, 2048(a1)` jumps to -2048.

**Function:** RISC-V assembler immediate encoding (U/I/S-type paths + CSR index)

**Detected by:** PBT round-26g RISC-V boundary battery (16 forms; the 5 silent-accepts above; every in-range form byte-identical to llvm-mc).

**Minimal input:**
```asm
.text
sb a0, 2048(a1)
```
```bash
ccc-riscv -c t.s -o t.o   # assembles!
llvm-mc -triple=riscv64 -filetype=obj t.s   # error: immediate must be an integer in range [-2048, 2047]
```

**Severity:** medium (silent wrong instruction — #796's class confirmed systemic across paths)

**Contract evidence:** inferred (ISA field widths; llvm-mc rejects every form; the encodings provably change semantics)

**Fix:** range-check every immediate slot per instruction format: U-type imm20 [0,65535] for lui/auipc (negative values require manual 2^20 arithmetic), I-type imm12 for jalr, S-type imm12 for stores, 12-bit unsigned CSR index for csrr* — mirror the imm12 check #796 already needs.

**Regression test:** deterministic: each of the five forms must be rejected.

title: Bug: AArch64 writeback addressing silently accepts offsets beyond the imm9 range — ldr x0, [x1, #504]! encodes garbage
body:
# Bug: AArch64 writeback addressing silently accepts offsets beyond the imm9 range

**Law:** Pre/post-index writeback addressing (`[xN, #imm]!` / `[xN], #imm`) uses the **imm9** field (signed 9-bit, **-256..255**), not the scaled imm12 of the plain offset form. An offset outside -256..255 is unencodable in a writeback form and must be rejected.

**Impact:** External `.s` files with writeback offsets in the 256..504 band (legal-looking because the NON-writeback `ldr x0, [x1, #504]` form allows them via imm12 scaling) silently assemble to a DIFFERENT instruction: `ldr x0, [x1, #504]!` encodes `20 8c 5f f8` — the imm9 field takes #504's low bits (504 & 0x1FF = 248), loading from `[x1, #248]` with writeback — the wrong address.

**Function:** AArch64 assembler load/store writeback encoding path

**Detected by:** PBT round-26f writeback boundary battery (byte-level vs llvm-mc; boundary identified between #255 valid and #504 invalid).

**Minimal input:**
```asm
.text
ldr x0, [x1, #504]!
```
```bash
ccc-arm -mlittle-endian -c t.s -o t.o && readelf -x .text t.o
# ccc: assembles, .text = 208c5ff8  (imm9 field garbage)
aarch64-linux-gnu-as t.s -o t.o    # error: 504 is out of range [-256,255]
```

**Expected:** error — imm9 range is [-256, 255]; the plain-offset form must be written without `!`.

**Actual:** silently assembled:
```console
$ readelf -x .text t.o
  0x00000000 208c5ff8
```
Decoding `0xF85F8C20`: imm9 = 0b011111000 = 248 → the instruction is `ldr x0, [x1, #248]!` — the wrong offset.

**Verified boundary:** `ldr x0, [x1, #255]!` is byte-identical to llvm-mc (`20fc4ff8` MATCH); the fault is only the range CHECK for writeback imm9, the encoding field itself is correct within range.

**Severity:** medium (silent wrong-address load — the #776/#792 class on the writeback path)

**Contract evidence:** inferred (double-reference rejection: aarch64-linux-gnu-as AND llvm-mc both reject; ARM ARM defines writeback imm9)

**Fix:** in the writeback (`!`/post-index) path, range-check the offset to [-256, 255] and error outside it; the non-writeback path keeps its imm12 check.

**Regression test:** deterministic: `ldr x0, [x1, #504]!` must be rejected; `ldr x0, [x1, #255]!` must assemble to `20fc4ff8`.

title: Bug: RISC-V assembler lacks part of the compressed (RVC) subset: c.lwsp/c.sw/c.beqz/c.slli rejected while c.add/c.mv/c.addi/c.li/c.jr work

title: Bug: x86 assembler's 'initial AVX-512' covers only unmasked VL forms — zmm (512-bit) entirely and all {​%k} mask-predication forms are rejected
body:
**Law:** the x86 README documents "initial AVX-512" support; GNU as and llvm-mc (with the matching -mattr) assemble the full EVEX surface.

**Impact:** external .s files using AVX-512 fail to assemble on: (a) ALL zmm (512-bit) register forms — vpxord/vpxorq/vpaddd/vpaddq/vmovdqu64/vaddpd/vmulps/vpermd/vpord/vpcmpeqd/vptestmd/vrndscalepd/vreduceps %zmm... (15/17 probe forms); (b) ALL mask-predication forms — `vpaddd %ymm0, %ymm1, %ymm2{%k1}`, `vaddpd %xmm..., %xmm..., %xmm2{%k1}{z}` (GNU as accepts; ccc rejects). What works: unmasked VL forms (`vpxord %xmm0, %xmm1, %xmm2`).

**Function:** x86 assembler EVEX encoder
**Source location:** src/backend/x86/assembler/encoder/avx.rs (EVEX path: zmm register-class + {%%k} mask operand syntax unhandled)
**Detected by:** round-26 AVX-512 battery (17 forms, double-reference: as ∧ llvm-mc -mattr=+avx512* accept, ccc rejects 15)
**Minimal input:** `.text\nvpaddd %zmm6, %zmm7, %zmm8` → ccc: rejected
**Expected:** assembles (README: "initial AVX-512")
**Actual:** rejected
**Severity:** low (completeness — the internal C pipeline never emits avx512; external-asm compat)
**Contract evidence:** documented — src/backend/x86/README.md:61 "covers ... initial AVX-512" (the shipped subset is narrower than any reading of "initial" that includes 512-bit registers, the feature's defining width)
**Fix:** extend the EVEX encoder to the zmm register class (LL'RC fields, 512-bit vector length) and parse the {%%k1}[{z}] mask suffix on any EVEX form.
**Regression test:** deterministic: assemble one zmm form and one masked VL form.

title: Bug: x87 assembler subset gaps: fst %st(i), fcomi, the whole fcmovcc family, fstsw/fsave/frstor aliases, ffree/fnop/fincstp/fdecstp
body:
**Law:** the assembler's documented x87 FPU coverage includes the standard instruction set; both GNU as and llvm-mc assemble every form below.

**Impact:** external .s files (hand-written math kernels, long-double code paths) fail to assemble. All double-reference confirmed (as AND llvm-mc accept, ccc rejects):
- `fst %st(i)` — non-popping store to a stack register (fstp works)
- `fcomi %st(i), %st` — ordered compare-and-set-flags (fcomip AND fucomi/fucomip work; only the base fcomi form is missing)
- `fcmovcc %st(i), %st` — the ENTIRE conditional-move family (b/e/be/u/nb/ne/nbe/nu — 8 conditions)
- `fstsw %ax` / `fstsw mem` — store-status-word alias (fnstsw works)
- `fsave`/`frstor` (fnsave/fnstenv-family aliases)
- `fincstp`/`fdecstp`/`ffree %st(i)`/`fnop`

**Function:** x86 assembler x87 encoder
**Source location:** src/backend/x86/assembler/encoder/x87_misc.rs (missing arms / no-wait-alias table incomplete)
**Detected by:** round-26 x87 battery (51 forms; 28+12 clean, 16 GAPs all in the listed families)
**Minimal input:** `.text\nfstsw %ax` (the classic fcom+fstsw+sahf compare idiom) → ccc rejects
**Expected:** assembles
**Actual:** rejected
**Severity:** low (completeness; same class as #777/#782/#818)
**Contract evidence:** inferred (double-reference acceptance; x86/README documents x87 FPU support)
**Fix:** add the missing arms: fst st(i) (D8 D0+i / DD D8+i), fcomi (DB F0+i), fcmovcc (DA C0+i / DB C0+i per condition), the wait-alias forms (fstsw=fnsaw alias 9B DF E0; fsave/fnsave 9B DD / DD), ffree (DD C0+i), fnop (D9 D0), fincstp/fdecstp (D9 F7 / F6).
**Regression test:** deterministic: assemble the six minimal forms.

title: Bug: x86 assembler lacks the SSE conversion/shuffle subset: cvtt*2si* entirely (reg and mem), cvtsi2*/pshuf* memory-source forms, maskmovq/maskmovdqu
body:
**Law:** the assembler's documented SSE coverage ("SSE through SSE4.1") includes the scalar conversion and shuffle instructions; both GNU as and llvm-mc assemble every form below.

**Impact:** external .s files using these forms fail to assemble. Scope (all double-reference confirmed: as AND llvm-mc accept, ccc rejects):

- `pshuflw/pshufhw/pshufd $imm, mem, %xmm` — memory-source forms (register forms work)
- `maskmovq %mm1, %mm2`, `maskmovdqu %xmm1, %xmm2` — missing entirely

**Function:** x86 assembler SSE encoder (conversion/shuffle subset)
**Source location:** src/backend/x86/assembler/encoder/sse.rs (cvtt family absent; cvtsi2*/pshuf* accept register sources only; no maskmov arm)
**Detected by:** round-26 memory-operand + conversion probe matrix (24 forms; the register-only round-15 families never generated memory sources)
**Minimal input:** `.text\ncvttss2si %xmm0, %eax` → ccc: unhandled; as+llvm-mc: assemble
**Expected:** assembles (SSE scalar conversion)
**Actual:** rejected
**Severity:** low (completeness; same class as #777/#782 — no wrong code)
**Contract evidence:** inferred (double-reference acceptance; x86/README "SSE through SSE4.1")
**Fix:** add the cvtt*2si{,q} arms (0F 2C/2D with 66/F2/F3 prefixes), memory-source parsing in the cvtsi2* and pshuf* arms, and the maskmovq/dqu arm (0F F7).

title: Bug: sema accepts same-scope enum redefinition (enum E { A }; enum E { A };) — C11 6.7.2.3 constraint violation
