**Law:** C11 6.7.2.3p3: a redeclaration of the same tag in the same scope without an intervening closing brace is a constraint violation — gcc: "error: nested redefinition of 'enum E'".

**Impact:** accepts-invalid: programs with accidental enum redefinitions (typically merge/hdr-include accidents) compile silently; if the two definitions DISAGREE (different values for the same name), later uses silently take one of the definitions — a silent wrong-constant risk.

**Function:** sema enum-declaration handling (same-scope redefinition check missing)
**Source location:** src/frontend/sema/analysis.rs (enum declaration path — the same area as #560/#561)
**Detected by:** round-24 second-loop sema battery (10 gcc -fsyntax-only differential cases; 9 agree, this one diverges)
**Minimal input:** `enum E { A };\nenum E { A };\nint main(void){return A;}` — gcc: error; ccc: compiles (exit 0)
**Expected:** error (nested redefinition)
**Actual:** accepted
**Severity:** low (accepts-invalid; distinct from #560 scope-shadow leak — that was cross-scope)
**Contract evidence:** inferred (C11 6.7.2.3; gcc rejects with the constraint diagnostic)
**Fix:** in the enum declaration path, reject a second enumerator-list definition of a tag already completed in the SAME scope (inner-scope shadowing remains legal, cf. #560's fix).
**Regression test:** deterministic: ccc -fsyntax-only on the minimal input must fail.

title: Bug: ccc-riscv -S output lacks the .attribute arch directive — external assemblers (llvm-mc/GNU as) reject it (fsd/mul need D/M declared)
body:
**Law:** an assembler source that uses instructions beyond the base ISA must declare the module set; GNU/LLVM assemblers default to rv64i and REQUIRE `.attribute arch, "rv64..."` (or -march) before accepting fsd (D) / mul (M) / float instructions. gcc/clang -S always emit the attribute.

**Impact:** ccc-riscv's -S output cannot be assembled by ANY external assembler (llvm-mc: "instruction requires 'D' / 'M'"), breaking the -S → external-tool → link workflow (asm inspection, hand-tuning, objdump roundtrips). The internal -c path is unaffected.

**Function:** riscv codegen -S emission
**Source location:** src/backend/riscv/ (-S output has no .attribute arch line; verified: grep -c attribute on -S output = 0)
**Detected by:** round-23 -S roundtrip differential (llvm-mc failed on ccc's own -S output; prepending `.attribute arch, "rv64gc"` fixes it)
**Minimal input:** compile any program using a double or multiplication with `ccc-riscv -S`; then `llvm-mc -triple=riscv64 -filetype=obj` on the .s → "error: instruction requires the following: 'D'"
**Expected:** .s starts with (or contains) `.attribute arch, "rv64gc"` (or the configured march)
**Actual:** no attribute line at all
**Severity:** low (interop; internal pipeline fine)
**Contract evidence:** inferred (both reference assemblers require it; the -march= flag exists on the CLI so the arch string is known at emit time)
**Fix:** emit `.attribute arch, "rv64<i|m|f|d...>"` at the top of -S output per the selected -march (default gc).

title: Bug: builtin x86 assembler encodes `movb $imm, %r8` in the 3-byte C6 form — never the 2-byte B0+ short form (1-byte bloat per mov-imm-to-8bit-reg)
body:
**Law:** x86 has a canonical short encoding for `mov $imm8, %al..%bl` etc. (opcode B0+r, 2 bytes); GNU as uses it. ccc's builtin assembler always emits the 3-byte C6 /0 form.

**Impact:** systematic code-size bloat: every mov-imm-to-8-bit-register in generated code is 1 byte larger than gcc's (found via the -S round-trip: ccc -S output assembled by GNU as produces SHORTER .text than ccc -c's own object — byte-identical otherwise). Not a correctness bug; affects all generated code density.

**Function:** x86 assembler mov-immediate encoder
**Source location:** src/backend/x86/assembler/encoder/gp_integer.rs:98/187 (`self.bytes.push(0xC6)` — no B0+r short-form arm for imm8→r8 without REX)
**Detected by:** round-22 -S round-trip differential (rt.c: direct -c .text = `... c6 c0 01 ...` vs GNU as on ccc's own -S output = `... b0 01 ...`; rest of the function byte-identical, shifted by the 1-byte delta)
**Minimal input:** `.text\nmovb $1, %al` → ccc: `c6 c0 01` (3B); as: `b0 01` (2B)
**Expected:** 2-byte B0+r form for non-REX 8-bit registers
**Actual:** 3-byte C6 /0 form always
**Severity:** low (code size only; execution identical)
**Contract evidence:** inferred (double-reference: GNU as encodes the short form for ccc's own emitted text)
**Fix:** in the imm8 path, when the destination is a legacy 8-bit register (no REX needed), emit B0+reg instead of C6 /0 ib.
**Regression test:** assemble `movb $1, %al` and assert the 2-byte encoding.

title: Bug: irconst_to_bits does a NUMERIC cast, not a bitcast — signbit(-0.0) folds to 0 on constants
body:
**Law:** the function's own documentation says it converts an IrConst "to raw u64 bits for bit-level operations" (src/common/README.md). A float constant's bit-level value is its IEEE 754 pattern: bits(-0.0) = 0x8000000000000000.

**Impact:** every compile-time-folded float bit operation is silently wrong. Visible symptom: `signbit(-0.0)` folds to 0 when the operand is a literal/local/computed constant (works correctly through a global variable's runtime load — the runtime bitcast path is fine). The pattern: `IrConst::F64(v) => *v as i64 as u64` converts the VALUE (-0.0 → 0, 3.5 → 3) instead of the bits. signbit(-3.5) survives only by accident (-3 >> 63 = 1); signbit(-0.0) is the canonical falsifier; any const bit-trick (union punning of const floats, frexp-style masks) is corrupted.

**Function:** shared_const_eval::irconst_to_bits
**Source location:** src/common/const_eval.rs:298-305 (`IrConst::F32(v) => *v as i64 as u64, IrConst::F64(v) => *v as i64 as u64`)
**Detected by:** round-22 battery (NaN/-0.0 semantics probe vs gcc; isolated: global=1, local/const/computed=0 at -O0 AND -O2; gcc gives 1 everywhere)
**Minimal input:** `double lit = -0.0; printf("%d %d\n", signbit(lit), signbit(-0.0));` → gcc: `1 1`; ccc -O0/-O2: `0 0` (signbit via glibc math.h → __builtin_signbit → the SignBit intrinsic's constant path)
**Expected:** bitcast semantics (f64::to_bits / f32::to_bits widened)
**Actual:** numeric cast (`as i64`) — -0.0 → 0, 3.5 → 3, inf saturates
**Severity:** medium (silent wrong constant for bit-level float folding)
**Contract evidence:** documented-and-violated — src/common/README.md: "IrConst-to-bits conversion (irconst_to_bits) — Converts an IrConst to raw u64 bits for bit-level operations."
**Fix:** `IrConst::F64(v) => v.to_bits()`, `IrConst::F32(v) => (v.to_bits() as u32) as u64` (sign-extend per the bool you already return); keep the integer arm as is.
**Regression test:** the minimal input above asserting signbit(-0.0)==1 in all four positions (global/local/computed/bare-const).

title: Bug: x86 tail-call optimization misses the common `return f(...)` shape whose result joins a shared epilogue label (deep self-recursion overflows at -O2)
body:
**Law:** the peephole documents tail call optimization ("Phase 5: tail call optimization (call+epilogue+ret -> epilogue+jmp)"); the canonical tail-call shape — `return f(args)` compiled as call + jmp-to-shared-epilogue — must be converted to a jmp, as gcc does.

**Impact:** deep tail recursion (1,000,000 frames) runs fine under gcc -O2 (converted to a loop/jmp) but SEGFAULTS under ccc -O2 (plain call kept): `long sumto(long n, long acc) { return n == 0 ? acc : sumto(n-1, acc+n); }` → gcc prints 500000500000; ccc -O2 exits 139. Program-visible behavioral difference on legal C.

**Function:** peephole passes/tail_call.rs — is_tail_call_candidate
**Source location:** src/backend/x86/codegen/peephole/passes/tail_call.rs:143-218 — the scan requires the epilogue (movq %rbp,%rsp + popq %rbp + ret) INLINE within 30 lines after the call; any intervening LineKind::Jump/Label (the shared-epilogue join emitted for the OTHER return path) returns None.
**Detected by:** round-21 exotic-C battery (tail-recursion probe) vs gcc -O2, asm-confirmed (ccc -O2 sumto: 48-byte frame + 5 callee-save pushes + `call sumto`; gcc -O2: frame-free loop/jmp)
**Minimal input:** the sumto above with main calling sumto(1000000, 0)
**Expected:** ccc -O2 converts the tail call (or at minimum survives 1M frames like gcc)
**Actual:** call kept → stack overflow (exit 139)
**Severity:** low (quality/stack-depth; no wrong result — pure crash at extreme depth) — filed because the feature is documented
**Contract evidence:** documented — src/backend/x86/codegen/peephole/README.md "| passes/tail_call.rs | ... Phase 5: tail call optimization (call+epilogue+ret -> epilogue+jmp) |"
**Fix:** in is_tail_call_candidate, follow a single unconditional jump to a local label (bounded, e.g. one hop) and validate the epilogue there; or make codegen emit the tail call's result path inline.
**Regression test:** (deterministic: compile sumto at -O2, disassemble, assert no `call sumto` inside sumto — or run depth 1M expecting exit 0)
**Related note (not filed):** -O0 frame bloat for the same function (48B + 5 callee-saves for 2 locals) halves the recursion depth vs gcc -O0 (ccc dies at 200k, gcc survives; both die at 400k) — already tracked in ideas/reduce_stack_frame_size*.txt.

title: Bug: RISC-V assembler silently accepts out-of-imm12-range immediates (addi a0, a1, 2048 encodes as -2048)
body:
**Law:** I-type immediates are SIGNED 12-bit: [-2048, 2047]; load/store offsets likewise. Out-of-range values are physically unencodable and must be rejected (the ISA field width is the contract — RISC-V unprivileged spec, imm[11:0]).

**Impact:** silent WRONG VALUE: `addi a0, a1, 2048` assembles with imm bits 0x800, which decodes as -2048 (verified by encoding bytes 13 85 05 80). Also affects andi/ori/xori (4096), addiw, ld/sd offsets (2048). llvm-mc rejects all; ccc accepts.

**Function:** RISC-V assembler immediate encoding
**Source location:** src/backend/riscv/assembler (no imm12 range validation)
**Detected by:** round-17 deep-sweep hand probes (11/15 invalid forms silently accepted); encoding bytes verified
**Minimal input:** `.text\naddi a0, a1, 2048` → encodes addi a0, a1, -2048
**Expected:** error (imm out of range)
**Actual:** silently encoded with truncated field — the wrong constant
**Severity:** medium (silent wrong value — worst class)
**Contract evidence:** inferred (ISA encoding field width: signed imm[11:0]; llvm-mc rejects; the encoding provably changes the value)
**Fix:** range-check every imm12 slot (addi/andi/ori/xori/slti*/addiw + load/store offsets) before packing.
**Regression test:** src/backend/riscv/mod.rs pbt_asm_deep (red witness)

title: Bug: AArch64 assembler silently accepts SP/WSP in register-file-only operand slots (and sp, sp, x28; mul w0, wsp, w2)
body:
**Law:** SP/WSP is only encodable in the dedicated SP-legal forms (add/sub immediate and shifted, loads/stores base, mov); logical ops, mul-family and most data-processing ops take X0-X30/W0-W30 only.

**Impact:** silent wrong encodings (SP encodes as reg 31 = XZR in those forms — `and sp, sp, x28` silently becomes `and xzr, xzr, x28`). Both references reject; ccc accepts.

**Detected by:** round-16 hand probe (`mul w0, wsp, w2`) + P1 domain finding (`and sp, sp, x28`); double-reference confirmed
**Minimal input:** `.text\nmul w0, wsp, w2`
**Severity:** medium
**Contract evidence:** inferred (double-reference)
**Fix:** reject SP/WSP operands outside the SP-legal opcode forms.
**Regression test:** (red witness to be added)

title: Bug: AArch64 assembler silently accepts invalid addressing forms (ldp non-multiple-of-8 offsets, ldr/str index scale lsl #4)
body:

**Impact:** silent wrong encodings. Both references reject; ccc accepts.

**Detected by:** round-16 hand probes (`ldp x0, x1, [sp, #3]`, `str x0, [x1, x2, lsl #4]`); double-reference confirmed

**Fix:** validate pair-offset alignment and index-scale bounds per access size.
**Regression test:** (red witness to be added)

**Expected:** error

title: Bug: x86 assembler silently coerces GPR operand width mismatches (movl %eax, %r8w assembles as r8d; addq %r10d, %r10 accepted)
body:
**Law:** an AT&T instruction form with a size suffix must reject operands whose register width disagrees with that suffix — `movl %eax, %r8w` has no encoding (16-bit dest in 32-bit mov).

**Impact:** hand-written or external .s files (asm sources, inline-asm edge cases) silently assemble to DIFFERENT instructions than written. Both GNU as and llvm-mc reject these forms; ccc accepts and encodes its own interpretation. ccc's internal C pipeline is unaffected (its codegen emits consistent forms — round-09 E2E vs gcc is fully green).

**Function:** x86 assembler parser/encoder (register-width validation absent)
**Source location:** src/backend/x86/assembler/parser.rs (operand parsing) — no width-vs-suffix check
**Detected by:** round-15 PBT, mutation class "width_swap", double-reference confirmed (GNU as exit 1 AND llvm-mc error; ccc exit 0 + object)
**Minimal input:** `.text\nmovl %eax, %r8w` → encodes `41 89 c0 (mov %eax,%r8d)`; also `addq %r10d, %r10`; also mem form `movl 596(%rsp), %r13`
**Expected:** error (both references reject)
**Actual:** silently assembled with the register reinterpreted at the opcode's width
**Severity:** medium
**Contract evidence:** inferred (double-reference convention: GNU as AND llvm-mc both reject; silent reinterpretation of the source text is a silent wrong-code path for external asm)
**Fix:** validate each register operand's width against the mnemonic suffix (and against the other operand) at parse time; error on mismatch.
**Regression test:** src/backend/x86/mod.rs pbt_regression_asm (test_x86asm_regression_gpr_width_rejected)

title: Bug: i686 target strips the arch-neutral gcc-internal include path — `#include <stdio.h>` fails out of the box on multilib hosts
body:
**Law:** switching targets must keep the compiler able to find the freestanding headers (stddef.h, stdarg.h). On a standard x86-64 multilib host their only source is `/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/<v>/include` — arch-NEUTRAL files that the i686 target can and must use.
**Impact:** `ccc -m32` / `ccc-i686` cannot compile ANY program that includes a glibc header (stdio.h pulls stddef.h/stdarg.h): "stddef.h: No such file or directory". The i686 target is unusable out of the box on the standard setup (gcc + gcc-multilib). Round 12's E2E property needed `-I /usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/10/include` to run at all.
**Function:** PredefinedMacros::set_target, "i686" | "i386" arm
**Source location:** /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler/src/frontend/preprocessor/predefined_macros.rs:187-190 (`system_include_paths.retain(|p| !p.contains("x86_64"))`) followed by the i686 path list (:191-202) whose cross dirs (`/usr/lib/gcc-cross/i686-linux-gnu/...`, `/usr/i686-linux-gnu/include`) do not exist on multilib hosts.
**Detected by:** round-12 E2E harness bring-up (compile failure, not a property mismatch)
**Minimal input:** `echo '#include <stdio.h>
int main(void){return 0;}' > t.c && ccc -m32 -o t t.c` → /usr/include/stdio.h:33:10: error: stddef.h: No such file or directory
**Expected:** compiles (like the x86-64 target does, finding the same file in /usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/<v>/include).
**Actual:** 2 preprocessor errors; the retain() removed the only dir containing stddef.h/stdarg.h.
**Severity:** medium (i686 target unusable out of the box; worked around by -I)
**Contract evidence:** inferred (freestanding headers are target-agnostic — gcc's own stddef.h is shared across -m32/-m64 on multilib hosts; the ARM/RISC-V arms legitimately swap cross dirs, but the i686 case runs ON the host gcc installation whose internal include dir is arch-neutral)
**Fix:** in the i686 arm, retain the gcc-INTERNAL dirs (only strip the multiarch `/usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu`), or append the existing `/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/<v>/include` dirs to the i686 list.
**Regression test:** (deterministic check) `ccc -m32` compiles `#include <stddef.h>` without -I — recorded in the round-12 harness comment; a unit regression needs the fixed path list (would assert set_target("i686") keeps a path that resolves stddef.h on the build host).

**Reproduction:**
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
printf '#include <stdio.h>\nint main(void){return 0;}\n' > /tmp/t32.c
PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo build --release
./target/release/ccc -m32 -o /tmp/t32 /tmp/t32.c
```
**Raw output:**
```
/usr/include/stdio.h:33:10: error: stddef.h: No such file or directory
/usr/include/stdio.h:36:10: error: stdarg.h: No such file or directory
ccc: error: 2 preprocessor error(s) in /tmp/t32.c
```

title: Bug: parse_integer_expr panics in debug on arithmetic overflow and out-of-range shifts instead of returning Err
body:
**Law:** `parse_integer_expr(s: &str) -> Result<i64, String>` has an error channel: any input the evaluator cannot handle must produce `Err`, never a panic. Detected during round 08's P8 differential (an unbounded generated expression hit the panic before the domain was bounded).

**Impact:** Debug builds panic (compiler crash on a malformed/oversized asm constant expression — e.g. a user macro computing `1 << 64` or a multiplication overflow in `.byte`/`.align`-style directives); release builds wrap silently — `1 << 64` evaluates to `1` (matches llvm-mc's silent wrap, but GNU `as` warns "shift count out of range" and yields 0). The debug/release divergence is itself a hazard: a constant that crashes a debug compiler silently changes value in release.

**Function:** `parse_integer_expr` (eval_tokens' mul/shift levels)
**Source location:** /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler/src/backend/asm_expr.rs:181 (`val *= eval_add(...)`, plain i64 `*=`); the shift level (`val <<= n`, `(val as u64) >> n` — plain shifts, no amount check)
**Detected by:** Differential (P8 p8_asmexpr_parse_matches_evaluator, round 08) — the initial failure "attempt to multiply with overflow" / "attempt to shift left with overflow"; extended into the deterministic red regression below.
**Minimal input:** `parse_integer_expr("9223372036854775807 * 9223372036854775807")` → debug panic; `parse_integer_expr("1 << 64")` → debug panic.
**Expected:** `Err(...)` for both.
**Actual:** debug panic (`attempt to multiply with overflow` / `attempt to shift left with overflow`); release wraps silently (1<<64 → 1).
**Severity:** low (debug-only panic; release matches llvm-mc's wrap but diverges from GAS's warn+0 — a warning or Err would be strictly better)
**Contract evidence:** inferred (the `Result` return type is the error contract: inputs the parser rejects must yield Err; every other invalid-input path — bad tokens, trailing junk, div-by-zero — already returns Err)
**Fix:** checked arithmetic in eval_tokens: `val.checked_mul(rhs).ok_or("multiplication overflow")?` and validate shift amounts `< 64` (or wrap with a GAS-style diagnostic); apply to both shift directions.
**Regression test:** src/backend/asm_expr.rs `pbt_regression::test_asmexpr_regression_arith_panic_not_err` (red witness)

**Reproduction:**
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test --lib backend::asm_expr::pbt_regression::test_asmexpr_regression_arith_panic_not_err --exact --nocapture
```

title: Bug: narrow Phase 2 rewrites I64 bitwise ops to I32 without checking the use — I64 consumers get the zero-extended value
body:
**Law:** A rewrite pass must preserve the value of the function it transforms (the pipeline's own contract: every pass preserves interpreted values; README pipeline overview). Narrowing `Or(sext(a), sext(b))` at I64 to `Or` at I32 is only value-preserving when the result is re-sign-extended to I64 at the consumer; with no re-extension the I64 consumer reads the zero-extended 32-bit pattern.
**Impact:** Pipeline-level silent miscompile: `f(a: i32, b: i32) -> i64 { Or((i64)a, (i64)b) }` compiled through run_passes(-O2, x86-64) returns 4294967295 for f(1, -1) instead of -1 (confirmed by interpreting the post-pipeline IR: `Or` survives at I32 feeding an I64 Return with no Cast). And/Xor share the code path (same missing use-check); on x86-64 a 32-bit result register move zero-extends. No C-level repro found with straightforward sources (the frontend emits Or-at-I32 + single cast for `(long long)a|(long long)b`), but any IR producer that emits the widen-widen-bitwise shape (e.g. future frontend paths, other pass interleavings, or LTO-style module input) is miscompiled by the documented pipeline.
**Function:** narrow_binops_without_cast (Phase 2)
**Source location:** /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler/src/passes/narrow.rs:264 (the rewrite at :346-356 checks use_counts == 1, operand narrowability and target width — never the USE's required type)
**Detected by:** Algebraic invariant — value preservation, property P13 (pipeline-confirmed via run_passes probe)

title: Bug: constant_fold's 32-bit fast path sign-extends sub-int operands before logical ops (LShr/UDiv/URem at I8/I16 fold wrong)
body:
**Law:** A BinOp typed I8/I16 denotes an operation on the 8/16-bit value domain: `LShr` is a LOGICAL shift of the zero-extended sub-int bit pattern. Folding `LShr((I8)0xB8, 1)` must yield 92.
**Impact:** Any I8/I16-typed logical shift / unsigned div / unsigned rem instruction that reaches constant_fold with a negative constant operand silently folds to the wrong constant (the sign bits dragged down into the result). The pipeline re-runs constant_fold after narrow has moved ops down to sub-int types (narrow Phase 1 targets the narrowing cast's type, including I8/I16), so this is a latent silent-miscompile path in `-O` pipelines.
**Function:** fold_binop (called from try_fold_with_map's `is_32bit` arms)
**Source location:** /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler/src/passes/constant_fold.rs:684 (fold_binop; LShr arm at :729, same pattern in UDiv/URem arms)
**Detected by:** Differential — P5 fold-vs-C11-interpreter over random all-constant DAGs at mixed widths
**Minimal input:** one-instruction function `d = LShr(Const(I8(-72)), Const(I8(1)), I8)`; return d. (Also `UDiv(Const(I8(-72)), Const(I8(2)), I8)`.)
**Expected:** 92 (0xB8 >>u 1 = 0x5C; 0xB8 /u 2 = 0x5C)
**Actual:** -36 (0xDC) — `(lhs as u32)` sign-extends the i8 -72 to 0xFFFFFFB8 before the logical shift; 0xFFFFFFB8 >> 1 low byte = 0xDC
**Severity:** medium (IR-level latent miscompile; no C-level repro found — the frontend promotes sub-int ops to I32/I64 before emitting shifts, and straightforward C sources do not emit an I8-typed LShr — but the optimizer's own narrow Phase 1 can create exactly that instruction shape and the next constant_fold iteration folds it wrong)
**Contract evidence:** inferred (the IrType-typed BinOp semantics: `ty` is the operation's value domain — the pass itself truncates operands to `ty` first (`ty.truncate_i64`), so the logical-op arms must also zero-extend within `ty`'s width; the `as u32`/`as i32` casts model the 32-bit types, not I8/I16)
**Fix:** In fold_binop's `is_32bit` logical arms, mask to the operand width before widening: for LShr/UDiv/URem use `((lhs as u64) & mask_of(ty)) as u32`-equivalent (zero-extend the sub-int pattern); AShr's `as i32` sign-extension is promotion-correct and can stay. Same fix needed for the UDiv and URem arms.
**Regression test:** src/passes/constant_fold.rs `pbt_tests::test_constant_fold_regression_subint_lshr_zero_extend` (red witness, also covers the UDiv form)

**Reproduction:**
```bash
cd /home/shuhao/fermat-users/leo/github/claudes-c-compiler
PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test --lib passes::constant_fold::pbt_tests::test_constant_fold_regression_subint_lshr_zero_extend --exact --nocapture
```

title: Bug: ir/constants.rs f64_to_f128_bytes/f64_to_x87_bytes mis-encode subnormals (~2^51× too large) — separate from long_double.rs paths
body:
# Bug: `f64_to_f128_bytes`/`f64_to_x87_bytes` (src/ir/constants.rs) mis-encode subnormals

**Law:** ∀ finite f64 v: decode(encode(v)) == v, where decode is the field-level IEEE 754 decoder built from the formats' own definitions (both target formats — binary128 and x87 80-bit — represent every f64 exactly, subnormals included: they become NORMAL numbers in the wider formats).

**Impact:** Any f64 subnormal literal that flows into a long double constant (`IrConst::LongDouble` path or long-double data emission) through the IR-local encoders is encoded ≈2^51 times too large (decoded 2^-1023-family instead of 2^-1074-family). On ARM64/RISC-V the f128 bytes are emitted verbatim → wrong data in .rodata; on x86 the bytes convert to a wrong x87 constant. `long double x = 5e-324;` and any underflowed constant expression are legal C.

**Function:** `f64_to_f128_bytes`, `f64_to_x87_bytes` — src/ir/constants.rs:50 and :82 (IR-local duplicates of the common/long_double.rs converters, with their own subnormal bug: no implicit-1 normalization, exponent field 15360 instead of 15361)

**Detected by:** Reference — independent IEEE 754 field decoder, property P7

**Minimal input:** `f64_to_f128_bytes(5e-324)`

**Expected:** the f128 encoding of 2^-1074 (normal f128, exponent field 15361)

**Actual:** exponent field 15360 with mantissa 2^60 and no implicit-1 normalization → decodes to ≈1.1125e-308 instead of 5e-324

**Severity:** medium (rare input class; silent wrong constant data when hit)

**Related:** #2 (panic path in common/long_double.rs `f64_to_f128_bytes_lossless`), #516 (x87 implicit-1 bug in common/long_double.rs `f64_to_x87_bytes_simple`), #517 (f128 truncation) — all in the sibling common/ module; this issue covers the separate IR-local encoder pair.

**Regression test:** `src/ir/constants.rs` `pbt_regression::test_ir_const_regression_subnormal_encoding` (intentionally red). Independently revalidated post-campaign.

title: Bug: IrConst::coerce_to keeps the forbidden I8/I16 variant for U8/U16 targets — early-return arm breaks the zero-extension storage convention
body:
# Bug: `IrConst::coerce_to` keeps the forbidden I8/I16 variant for U8/U16 targets

**Law:** Coercing a constant to an unsigned sub-64-bit type must yield the zero-extended representation (`to_i64()` reads back the unsigned value): `from_i64(v, I8)` followed by `.coerce_to(U8)` and `from_i64(v, U8)` are two writers of the same "U8 constant with value v" and must agree (the convention documented on `from_i64`, src/ir/constants.rs:437).

**Impact:** Coercion is the universal "match the constant to the instruction type" step in the optimizer; for values above the signed range (U8 128–255, U16 32768–65535) the coerced constant reads back negative through `to_i64()`, corrupting constant folding (e.g. signed→unsigned assignment/conversion of constants). Note `narrowed_to` (constants.rs:579) already implements the correct behavior — the two same-job functions disagree.

**Function:** `IrConst::coerce_to_with_src` (and wrapper `coerce_to`) — src/ir/constants.rs:384

**Detected by:** Differential — same-job writers (from_i64 vs coerce_to), property P6

**Minimal input:** `IrConst::from_i64(200, IrType::I8).coerce_to(IrType::U8)`

**Expected:** `to_i64() == Some(200)` (I64(200) per the convention)

**Actual:** `IrConst::I8(-56)`, `to_i64() == Some(-56)` — the `(IrConst::I8(_), IrType::I8 | IrType::U8) => return *self` early-return arm keeps the forbidden variant

**Severity:** high

**Related:** #3 (same storage convention violated by the float-cast writer; this issue is the coerce_to writer — a different defect site needing its own fix)

**Regression test:** `src/ir/constants.rs` `pbt_regression::test_ir_const_regression_coerce_u8_early_return` (intentionally red). Independently revalidated post-campaign.

title: Bug: compute_dominance_frontiers misses the entry block when entry is in a cycle — DF(entry) never contains entry (Cytron violation)
body:
# Bug: `compute_dominance_frontiers` misses the entry block when entry is in a cycle

**Law:** Per Cytron et al. 1991, DF_local(n) = {y ∈ succ(n) : n does not strictly dominate y}; equivalently DF(b) ∋ d iff b dominates a pred of d and b does not strictly dominate d. When the entry block is in ANY cycle (direct self-edge 0→0, or longer 0→…→p→0 with 0 dominating p), entry ∈ DF(entry).

**Impact:** Phi placement (mem2reg step 5) inserts phis at the iterated dominance frontiers of def blocks. With DF(entry) never containing entry, a variable stored inside such an entry cycle gets no phi at entry: the load placed before the store reads the initial zero every iteration instead of the previous iteration's value — a silent miscompile of the loop-carried value. Reachability today: the C frontend never targets the entry block, so this requires direct IR construction or a future pass that redirects a back edge into the entry block (e.g. block merging in cfg_simplify). Severity capped at low for that reason; the algorithm's contract violation is unconditional.

**Function:** `compute_dominance_frontiers` — src/ir/analysis.rs:302

**Detected by:** Reference — set-definition checker (property P11; deterministic witness p11b)

**Minimal input:** single block, succs = [[0]] (entry self-loop); or 0→1, 1→{0,1}

**Expected:** DF(0) ∋ 0

**Actual:** DF(0) = {} — two compounding causes: (1) the `preds.len(b) < 2 → continue` join gate skips single-pred blocks, and (2) the runner walk stops at idom[entry] == entry

**Severity:** low (documented-unreachable from today's C lowering; filed for the definitional violation and future-pass hazard)

**Regression test:** `src/ir/analysis.rs` `pbt_tests::p11b_entry_selfloop_df` (intentionally red witness, both cycle forms). Independently revalidated post-campaign.

title: Bug: build_cfg pushes duplicate predecessors for CondBranch/Switch with equal targets — preds/succs CSR transpose invariant violated
body:
# Bug: `build_cfg` pushes duplicate predecessors for CondBranch/Switch with equal targets

**Law:** `build_cfg` returns ONE control flow graph as a (preds, succs) CSR pair; the two adjacency lists must be exact transposes of each other with no duplicate entries: ∀ i,b: i ∈ succs[b-row] ⇔ b ∈ preds[i-row], with equal multiplicity.

**Impact:** CondBranch with true_label == false_label and Switch with duplicate case targets (both representable IR; `case 1: case 2:` in C naturally produces duplicate switch labels) push the predecessor entry once per label while the successor entry is deduplicated. Every consumer that counts predecessors is corrupted: `if_convert.rs:305/386` (`preds.len(...) != 2` diamond detection), GVN's join detection (`gvn.rs:439 preds.len > 1`), mem2reg's dominance-frontier join gate and phi-copy cost estimate. Today the effects are masked, but the data-structure invariant that six passes build on is violated — a latent correctness trap.

**Function:** `build_cfg` — src/ir/analysis.rs:110 (the `preds[f].push(i32)` in the CondBranch arm runs unconditionally while the succs push is guarded by `contains`; same in the Switch and IndirectBranch arms)

**Detected by:** Algebraic invariant (transpose consistency), property P9

**Minimal input:** block0: `CondBranch{cond: 1, true: L1, false: L1}`; block1: Return

**Expected:** succs[0] = [1], preds[1] = [0]

**Actual:** succs[0] = [1], preds[1] = [0, 0]

**Severity:** medium

**Regression test:** `src/ir/analysis.rs` `pbt_regression::test_ir_analysis_regression_build_cfg_dup_preds` (intentionally red). Independently revalidated post-campaign.

title: Bug: constant folding of unary minus on unsigned doesn't wrap — -((unsigned)(0) + (-1)) folds to -4294967295 instead of 1
body:
# Bug: constant folding of unary minus on unsigned doesn't wrap mod 2^width

**Law:** `-x` for unsigned x computes the unsigned negation, modulo 2^width (gcc 9.4 folds `-((unsigned)(0 + -1))` to `1u`).

**Impact:** Any compile-time constant built by negating an unsigned expression — enum values, array sizes, static initializers — gets a negative value instead of the wrapped unsigned one: `enum { X = -((unsigned)(0 + -1)) }` becomes -4294967295 instead of 1.

**Function:** `SemaConstEval::eval_const_expr` (UnaryOp::Neg path) — src/frontend/sema/const_eval.rs:103

title: Bug: TypeContext undo-log resurrects same-scope double inserts — typedef int T; typedef long T; leaks T=long past the scope
body:
# Bug: `TypeContext` undo-log resurrects same-scope double inserts

**Law:** Re-inserting a key within ONE scope must not make that key survive the scope's exit: on pop, the key's pre-scope value (or absence) must be restored.

**Impact:** `void f(void){ typedef int T; typedef long T; }` leaks `T = long` past the function scope (should be absent/outer value). Same-scope redefinitions are accepted by design ("information gathering, not strict checking", README), so the undo-log must handle them; instead the second insert records the FIRST INSERT'S OWN value as a "shadowed outer value" and pop re-inserts it. Affects typedefs, typedef_alignments, struct_layouts, and ctype_cache paths (all four share the pattern).

**Function:** `TypeContext::insert_typedef_alignment_scoped` (+ same pattern in `insert_typedef_scoped`, `insert_struct_layout_scoped`, `insert_struct_layout_scoped_from_ref`, `invalidate_ctype_cache_scoped`) — src/frontend/sema/type_context.rs:461

**Detected by:** State machine — layered-scope model, invariant checked after every op (property P4)

**Minimal input:** ops `[push_scope, insert_align("kB",0), insert_align("kB",0), pop_scope]` → `typedef_alignments` still contains `kB`

**Expected:** `kB` absent after pop (it did not exist before push)

**Actual:** `kB == Some(0)` after pop — the scope's own value resurrected

**Severity:** medium

**Regression test:** `src/frontend/sema/type_context.rs` `pbt_regression::test_typecontext_regression_double_insert_resurrection` (intentionally red). Independently revalidated post-campaign.

title: Bug: shadowed enum constant leaks out of its scope — inner E=2 survives pop_scope and pollutes later file-level constants

# Bug: shadowed enum constant leaks out of its scope after `pop_scope`

**Law:** A scope's enum-constant definitions are undone when the scope closes (`pop_scope` doc: "undo changes to enum_constants, struct_layouts, ctype_cache, and typedefs").

**Impact:** Any later function/constants in the TU silently see the leaked inner value: `enum { E = 1 }; void f(void){ enum { E = 2 }; } enum { F = E + 0 };` yields F == 2 instead of 1 — a silent wrong compile-time constant for the rest of the file.

**Function:** `TypeContext::insert_enum_scoped` / `TypeContext::pop_scope` (via `SemanticAnalyzer::analyze`) — src/frontend/sema/type_context.rs:422

**Detected by:** Differential — layered-scope model through the real pipeline (property P5)

**Minimal input:** `enum { E = 1 }; void f(void) { enum { E = 2 }; } enum { F = E + 0 };`

**Expected:** `enum_constants["F"] == 1`

**Actual:** `enum_constants["F"] == 2` — root cause: `insert_enum_scoped` records only FIRST-insert keys in `frame.enums_added` (`!contains_key` guard); a key shadowing an outer value is never recorded, so pop never restores the outer value

**Severity:** high

title: Bug: usual_arithmetic_conversion types unsigned long + long long as SIGNED LongLong (C11 6.3.1.8 requires ULongLong)

# Bug: `usual_arithmetic_conversion` types `unsigned long + long long` as SIGNED `LongLong`

**Law:** C11 6.3.1.8: in usual arithmetic conversions, when the higher-ranked signed type cannot represent all values of the unsigned operand (same width, 64-bit LP64), the result must be the UNSIGNED counterpart of that signed type.

**Impact:** Every mixed `unsigned long`/`size_t` ↔ `long long` expression — comparisons, division, shifts — is computed in SIGNED semantics by sema's ExprTypeChecker (and the same `usual_arithmetic_conversion` is used lower in the pipeline), so constants like `(size_t)0 - 1 + ll` compare `>= 0` and divide/shift differently than gcc. Common in kernel-style size arithmetic.

**Function:** `CType::usual_arithmetic_conversion` (reached via `ExprTypeChecker::infer_binop_ctype`) — src/common/types.rs:1576

**Detected by:** Differential — independent C11 6.3.1.8 model + gcc 9.4 semantics check (property P1, 1024 cases)

**Minimal input:** `unsigned long a; long long b; int p = a + b;` → `expr_types[p] == LongLong`

**Expected:** `ULongLong`

**Actual:** `LongLong`

**Severity:** high

title: Bug: empty-bodied macro expansion glues adjacent tokens — -EMPTY- becomes "--" instead of "- -" (also ++, //, <<)

# Bug: empty-bodied macro expansion glues adjacent tokens — `-EMPTY-` becomes `--`

**Law:** Expanding an empty-bodied macro must still occupy a token position: gcc emits a separating space at the expansion site, so `-EMPTY-` preprocessed is `- -` (two `-` tokens). The SUT's anti-paste guard `append_with_paste_guard` returns early when the expansion is empty (`if expanded.is_empty() { return; }`), so the surrounding `-` `-` are glued into a single `--` token.

**Impact:** Silent token mutation in the output fed to the lexer/parser: decrement becomes `--`, `+EMPTY+` becomes `++`, `/EMPTY/` becomes `//` (a comment start!), `<EMPTY<` becomes `<<`. Empty helper macros are a standard sequencing idiom; any use adjacent to operator tokens changes program meaning with no diagnostic.

**Function:** `MacroTable::append_with_paste_guard` — src/frontend/preprocessor/macro_defs.rs:253

**Detected by:** Differential — gcc 9.4 token-stream KAT (property P8b); predicted by P8's grammar

**Minimal input:** `#define EMPTY` then the line `-EMPTY-`

**Expected:** tokens `[-, -]` (gcc -E -P)

**Actual:** tokens `[--]`

**Severity:** medium

title: Bug: g(fmt, ## __VA_ARGS__) with an explicitly empty trailing argument drops the comma — VAC(a, ) expands to g(a) instead of g(a, )
body:
# Bug: `g(fmt, ## __VA_ARGS__)` with an explicitly empty trailing argument drops the comma

**Law:** The GNU comma-swallow extension `g(fmt, ## __VA_ARGS__)` removes the comma only when the variadic arguments are **entirely absent** (`VAC(a)`); when an (empty) variadic argument is explicitly supplied (`VAC(a, )`), the comma must survive — gcc 9.4 keeps it.

**Impact:** Any macro invocation that explicitly passes an empty trailing argument (common in generated code and wrapper macros) silently changes its expansion arity: `g(a, )` becomes `g(a)` — downstream C parses differently (wrong argument count), no diagnostic.

**Function:** `MacroTable::handle_stringify_and_paste` (with `MacroTable::get_va_args`) — src/frontend/preprocessor/macro_defs.rs:856 (comma-delete site), :1121 (`get_va_args`)

**Detected by:** Differential — gcc 9.4 token-stream differential (property P8, 1000+ cases)

**Minimal input:** `#define VAC(fmt, ...) g(fmt, ## __VA_ARGS__)` then `VAC(a, )`

**Expected:** `g(a, )` — tokens `[g ( a , )]` (gcc -E -P)

**Actual:** `g(a)` — tokens `[g ( a )]` — `get_va_args` collapses "one empty argument" into the same `""` as "no arguments", and the `##` handler then deletes the comma

**Severity:** medium

**Regression test:** `src/frontend/preprocessor/pipeline.rs` `pbt_regression::test_preprocess_regression_va_args_empty_arg_keeps_comma` (fails today; also caught by P8 gcc differential). Independently revalidated post-campaign (12 pass / 3 bug families).

# Bug: unterminated block comment leaks its last byte as a token

**Law:** A block comment `/* ... ` without a terminator consumes everything to end-of-file (C11 6.4.9p3: unterminated comment — GCC errors "unterminated comment" after consuming the rest of the file); in no case does comment content become tokens.

**Impact:** `int /* gone` lexes to `[Int, Identifier("e"), Eof]` — the comment's **last byte** (`e` from "gone") escapes as an identifier token. Combined with the missing diagnostic this silently changes program shape.

**Function:** `Lexer` block-comment scanning (src/frontend/lexer/scan.rs)

**Detected by:** Algebraic — comment swallowing invariant (everything from `/*` to EOF produces only the preceding tokens + Eof) over generated comments, 1000+ cases, shrunk

**Minimal input:** `int /* gone`

**Expected:** `[Int, Eof]` (plus ideally an "unterminated comment" diagnostic like GCC)

**Actual:** `[Int, Identifier("e"), Eof]`

**Severity:** medium

**Regression test:** `src/frontend/lexer/scan.rs` `pbt_regression::test_lex_comment_regression_unterminated_leaks_last_byte` (fails today: left `[Int, Identifier("e"), Eof]`, right `[Int, Eof]`). Independently revalidated post-campaign.

# Bug: run of unknown non-ASCII characters recurses per character in lex_punctuation — stack overflow (SIGABRT)

**Law:** `tokenize(s)` must terminate for every input string (the lexer API has no error channel; the in-code comment at the branch states the intent is to *continue* tokenizing, not recurse once per character).

**Impact:** Robustness/DoS — a ~3 KB run of non-ASCII garbage bytes (invalid C, but silently accepted input today; e.g. a UTF-8 blob or mis-encoded source outside comments/strings) aborts the whole compiler with SIGABRT (`fatal runtime error: stack overflow`) instead of skipping. Measured threshold on this machine: 2000 chars OK, 4000 chars crash (2 MiB thread stack).

**Function:** `Lexer::lex_punctuation` unknown-character branch (src/frontend/lexer/scan.rs:1173)

**Detected by:** Crash-only (termination contract) + isolated depth probes (1..2000 chars terminate; 200_000-char witness aborts)

**Minimal input:** `"\u{00FF}".repeat(4000)`

**Expected:** `tokenize` terminates and ends with `Eof`

**Actual:** `fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting` (SIGABRT) — one `next_token()` recursion per unknown character

**Severity:** medium (input is invalid C, but acceptance-today + process abort makes the compiler unusable on such files)

# Bug: 17-hex-digit integer literal silently lexes to 0 instead of wrapping mod 2^64

**Law:** An integer literal whose value does not fit in the chosen type follows C11 6.4.4.1p3 (no representable type → diagnostic) or, as GCC does for hex constants, wraps modulo 2^64 with at most a warning; producing **0** for `0x10000000000000001` matches neither.

**Impact:** `0x10000000000000001` (true value 2^64+1) silently lexes to 0 — an off-by-2^64 value corruption with no diagnostic.

**Function:** `Lexer` integer literal scanning (src/frontend/lexer/scan.rs)

**Detected by:** Algebraic — value identity (lit → u128 → wrap mod 2^64) over generated literals, 1000+ cases, shrunk

**Minimal input:** `0x10000000000000001`

**Expected:** `IntLiteral(1)` (2^64+1 mod 2^64; GCC: warning + value 1)

**Actual:** `IntLiteral(0)`

**Severity:** medium

**Regression test:** `src/frontend/lexer/scan.rs` `pbt_regression::test_lex_int_regression_u64_overflow_zero` (fails today: left `IntLiteral(0)`, right `IntLiteral(1)`). Independently revalidated post-campaign.

## Found by

```bash
pi-pbt build-run --provider zai-coding-cn --model glm-5.3 --lang en \
  --build-cmd 'PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo check --lib' \
  --scope src/frontend/lexer --out pbt-out/rounds/02_lexer --effort standard
```

title: Bug: lexer hex-float exponent truncated to i32 — 0x1p4294967296 lexes as 1.0 instead of inf, 0x1p-4294967296 as 1.0 instead of 0.0
body:
# Bug: lexer hex-float exponent truncated to i32 — 0x1p4294967296 lexes as 1.0 instead of inf

**Law:** A hex-float exponent is a decimal integer of unbounded magnitude; the value is `mantissa × 2^exp` computed in floating point (strtod semantics), so `0x1p4294967296` is +inf and `0x1p-4294967296` is +0.0.

**Impact:** Exponents ≥ 2^31 (or ≤ −2^31) wrap through an i32 and silently produce 1.0 (exp ≡ 0 mod 2^32) or other arbitrary small values instead of inf/0.0.

**Function:** `Lexer` hex-float exponent parsing (src/frontend/lexer/scan.rs)

**Detected by:** Algebraic — value identity vs strtod reference (property over generated exponents, 1000+ cases, shrunk to exp = 2^32)

**Minimal input:** `0x1p4294967296` and `0x1p-4294967296`

**Expected:** +inf and +0.0 respectively

**Actual:** 1.0 and 1.0

**Severity:** medium

**Regression test:** `src/frontend/lexer/scan.rs` `pbt_regression::test_lex_hex_float_regression_exponent_truncation` (fails today). Independently revalidated post-campaign.

title: Bug: lexer hex-float literal with a full 64-bit mantissa evaluates to 0.0 — 0x10000000000000000p0 (2^64) → 0.0
body:
# Bug: lexer hex-float literal with a full 64-bit mantissa evaluates to 0.0

**Law:** C99 hex floating literals (`0x1p0` form) must be converted to the nearest representable double (strtod semantics; GCC accepts `0x10000000000000000p0` = 2^64 without complaint — exactly representable in f64).

**Impact:** Every hex-float literal whose hex mantissa needs more than 64 bits before normalization silently lexes to `0.0` — silent wrong-code in any program using exact hex constants (common in math/kernel code).

**Function:** `Lexer` hex-float scanning (src/frontend/lexer/scan.rs)

**Detected by:** Algebraic — value identity vs strtod reference (property over generated hex-float literals, 1000+ cases, shrunk)

**Minimal input:** `0x10000000000000000p0` (mantissa = 2^64, exactly representable f64 18446744073709551616.0)

**Expected:** `FloatLiteral(18446744073709551616.0)`

**Actual:** `FloatLiteral(0.0)`

**Severity:** high

**Regression test:** `src/frontend/lexer/scan.rs` `pbt_regression::test_lex_hex_float_regression_wide_mantissa_zero` (fails today; `cargo test --lib lex_ -- --exact` reproduces: left `FloatLiteral(0.0)`, right `FloatLiteral(1.8446744073709552e19)`). Independently revalidated post-campaign.

title: Bug: encode_neon_ld_st_single accepts a non-consecutive register list
body:
# Bug: encode_neon_ld_st_single accepts a non-consecutive register list
**Law:** ARM ISA requires the registers in an LD/ST single-structure list to be consecutive (wrapping); a gap must be Err.
**Impact:** `st2 {v0.b, v2.b}[0], [x0]` encodes as `{v0.b, v1.b}` (only regs[0] is used), so a non-sequential list silently stores the wrong second register.
**Function:** encode_neon_ld_st_single
**Detected by:** Negative/error contract
**Minimal input:** encode_neon_ld_st_single([RegListIndexed({v0.b, v2.b}[0]), Mem{x0,0}], is_load=false, num_structs=2) returns Ok.
**Expected:** Err
**Actual:** Ok — only regs[0] supplies Rt; v2 is ignored. neon.rs:918 TODO admits the check is missing.
**Severity:** low
**Regression test:** src/backend/arm/assembler/encoder/encode_neon_ld_st_single_pbt.rs test_encode_neon_ld_st_single_regression_nonconsecutive

title: Bug: __builtin_bswap32 constant folding stores sign-extended I32 instead of zero-extended U32
body:
# Bug: __builtin_bswap32 constant folding stores sign-extended I32 instead of zero-extended U32

**Law:** `__builtin_bswap32(x)` is an unsigned-int function (GCC semantics); its folded constant must carry the unsigned value 0..2^32−1 zero-extended — which is the module's own representation rule for unsigned 32-bit results (`src/common/const_arith.rs:88-96`).

**Impact:** Constant folding of expressions like `__builtin_bswap32(v) | (1LL << 40)` reads the constant as sign-extended i64. The i128 widening path (`eval_const_binop_i128`: `rhs.to_i64()? as u64 as u128` with `rhs_unsigned = true`) sign-extends the I32(−n) through `to_i64` and produces a wildly wrong `__int128` value (0xFFFFFFFFFFBBD010 instead of 0xFFBBD010 for the witness).

**Function:** `eval_builtin_call` (bswap32 arm) (src/common/const_eval.rs:95)

**Detected by:** Reference differential — GCC semantics via Rust `swap_bytes` (property P12b, 1024 proptest cases)

**Minimal input:** `__builtin_bswap32(v)` with v = −5495501120125551105 (low u32 after bswap = 0xFFBBD010 ≥ 2^31)

**Expected:** folded constant 4290586368 (0xFFBBD010, zero-extended)

**Actual:** folded constant −4380928 (I32 sign-extended)

**Severity:** medium (documented representation rule violated)

**Regression test:** `src/common/const_eval.rs` `pbt_regression::test_eval_builtin_bswap32_regression_unsigned_repr` (`#[ignore]`d deterministic witness): `cargo test --lib -- --ignored` → `left: Some(-4380928), right: Some(4290586368)`. Independently revalidated post-campaign on the working tree (fails as described).

title: Bug: f128_bytes_to_f64 truncates instead of round-to-nearest — long-double constants up to 1 ulp low on ARM64/RISC-V
body:
# Bug: f128_bytes_to_f64 truncates instead of round-to-nearest — long-double constants up to 1 ulp low on ARM64/RISC-V

**Law:** Two same-job narrowings to f64 (direct x87→f64, documented round-to-nearest; and x87→f128→f64 across an exact widening) must produce the identical f64. IEEE-754 narrowing is round-to-nearest-even.

**Impact:** Compile-time `long double` arithmetic on ARM64/RISC-V folds constants up to 1 ulp **low** whenever the dropped 60 mantissa bits are ≥ half an ulp (≈50% of random mantissas). Affects `eval_const_binop_float`'s approx slot (`src/common/const_arith.rs:174-190`) and any `f128_bytes_to_f64` consumer. Witness differential: direct=3.2257192316651656e-151 via_f128=3.225719231665165e-151.

**Function:** `f128_bytes_to_f64` (src/common/long_double.rs:906)

**Detected by:** Differential — same-job sibling converters (property P10, 1024 proptest cases; siblings: `x87_bytes_to_f64` [round-to-nearest, correct] vs `f128_bytes_to_f64` [truncating, buggy])

**Minimal input:** x87 value 2^0 × 1.111…1 (all 64 mantissa bits set): `bytes[..8] = u64::MAX.to_le_bytes()`, `bytes[8..10] = {0xFF, 0x3F}`

**Expected:** f64 2.0 (round-to-nearest carries into the exponent — matches `x87_bytes_to_f64` and hardware/libm)

**Actual:** 1.9999999999999998 (truncated)

**Severity:** medium

**Regression test:** `src/common/long_double.rs` `pbt_regression::test_f128_bytes_to_f64_regression_truncation` (`#[ignore]`d deterministic witness): `cargo test --lib -- --ignored` → `left: 4611686018427387903, right: 4611686018427387904`. Independently revalidated post-campaign on the working tree (fails as described).

title: Bug: f64_to_x87_bytes_simple mis-encodes subnormal doubles — 5e-324 decodes back as +0.0
body:
# Bug: f64_to_x87_bytes_simple mis-encodes subnormal doubles — 5e-324 decodes back as +0.0

**Law:** Widening f64 → x87 80-bit is exact ("zero-fills the extra mantissa bits" per the function's own doc), so narrowing back must be bitwise lossless for **every** finite f64, subnormals included.

**Impact:** Any subnormal `double` constant converted through this path on x86/i686 (long-double constant folding, x87 FPU constant setup) becomes a completely different value (≈2.22e-308 instead of 5e-324, which then decodes to +0.0) — silent wrong-code, no diagnostic.

**Function:** `f64_to_x87_bytes_simple` (src/common/long_double.rs:1143)

**Detected by:** Algebraic — Round-trip (property P11, 1024 proptest cases, shrunk to bits=1)

**Minimal input:** `f64_to_x87_bytes_simple(f64::from_bits(1))` (5e-324)

**Expected:** round-trips back to 5e-324 (bits 0x1)

**Actual:** decodes to +0.0 (bits 0x0) — the encoder assumes an implicit leading mantissa 1 that subnormals do not have

**Severity:** high

**Regression test:** `src/common/long_double.rs` `pbt_regression::test_f64_to_x87_bytes_simple_regression_subnormal` (`#[ignore]`d deterministic witness): `cargo test --lib -- --ignored` → `left: 0, right: 1`. Independently revalidated post-campaign on the working tree (fails as described).

**Related:** #2 (same file `long_double.rs`, but different function and different failure mode: #2 is the F128-arm panic at :1040; this is the x87-arm silent mis-encode at :1143 — no panic).

**Impact:** Valid `ld1r {v0.8b}, [x0], x0` is assembled as no-writeback `ld1r {v0.8b}, [x0]`. Post-index address arithmetic is dropped, so subsequent loads use the old base.
**Function:** encode_neon_ld1r
**Detected by:** Differential vs llvm-mc
**Minimal input:** encode_neon_ld1r([RegList({v0.8b}), Mem{x0, 0}, Reg("x0")]) → 0x0d40c000 (no-offset). llvm-mc 0x0dc0c000.
**Expected:** 0x0dc0c000 (L=1, Rm=0)
**Actual:** 0x0d40c000 — third operand ignored; always Rm=11111 only for MemPostIndex.
**Severity:** high
**Regression test:** src/backend/arm/assembler/encoder/encode_neon_ld1r_pbt.rs test_encode_neon_ld1r_regression_reg_post

title: Bug: ccc-i686 -static emits entry = main with no C runtime — every static i686 binary crashes
body:
# Bug: ccc-i686 -static emits entry = main with no C runtime — every static i686 binary crashes at startup

**Law:** A statically linked executable's ELF entry point must be the runtime start function (`_start`), which sets up the stack/ABI environment, calls `main(argc, argv, envp)`, and terminates via the exit syscall with `main`'s return value. Emitting `main` itself as the entry is never valid: at process entry the stack top holds argc/argv, so `main`'s epilogue `ret` pops argc as a return address.

**Impact:** Every program compiled with `ccc -static` on the i686 backend segfaults immediately at startup, on any i686 environment (environment-independent — reproduced under qemu-i386 user-mode emulation). Exit status is 139 (SIGSEGV) instead of the program's return value. The x86-64 backend is unaffected (verified: `-static` links a proper `_start`); other backends untested.

**Function:** i686 standalone linker / static link pipeline (entry-point selection + crt0 selection)

**Detected by:** manual verification of issue #4 (fermat-hkrc/claudes-c-compiler#4) — needed a runnable static i686 binary to test cast codegen at runtime.

**Minimal input:**
```c
int main(void){return 7;}
```
```bash
ccc-i686 -static t7.c -o t7 && qemu-i386-static ./t7; echo $?   # → SIGSEGV, exit 139
```

**Expected:** program runs and exits 7. ELF entry points at a `_start` routine; the executable segment contains startup code plus `main`.

**Actual:** the binary crashes before reaching any program logic:

```console
$ readelf -h t7 | grep Entry
  Entry point address:               0x8049000
$ readelf -l t7 | grep "R E"
  LOAD           0x001000 0x08049000 0x08049000 0x00010 0x00010 R E 0x1000
```

The executable segment is exactly **0x10 = 16 bytes**, and disassembly of the entry is `main` itself with no runtime:

```
0:  55                   push   %ebp
1:  89 e5                mov    %esp,%ebp
3:  83 ec 08             sub    $0x8,%esp
6:  b8 07 00 00 00       mov    $0x7,%eax        ; return 7
b:  89 ec                mov    %ebp,%esp
d:  5d                   pop    %ebp
e:  c3                   ret                      ; pops argc (=1) → jumps to address 1 → SIGSEGV
```

No `_start`, no crt0, no exit syscall; the RW LOAD segment has FileSiz 0 (no data/bss support either).

**Root cause (probable):** the i686 static link path selects the `main` symbol as the ELF entry and links no startup object. The x86-64 static path links a real `_start` (verified: entry code is `endbr64; xor ebp,ebp; pop rsi; …`), so the defect is specific to the i686 static pipeline.

**Severity:** high (feature completely broken: any `-static` build on i686 is unusable)

**Regression test / verification harness:** a runtime probe can avoid both this bug and libc entirely by exiting via `int $0x80` inline asm (entry still lands on `main`, which then never returns) — that pattern is how issue #4's runtime verification was performed (`/tmp/i4_syscall.c` in the issue #4 verification record: `pbt-out/verified_bug/issue#4_Ptr_not_treated_as_unsigned_for_float_casts.md`).

**Related:** issue #4 (discovered during its verification). Environment note for reproducers: on hosts without 32-bit libc, *dynamic* ccc-i686 binaries also fail (missing loader deps) — use `qemu-i386-static`, which reproduces this bug in isolation.

## Found by

Manual verification of [issue #4](https://github.com/fermat-hkrc/claudes-c-compiler/issues/4) during issue triage (session workflow; original issue #4 was found by the PBT campaign below):

```bash
/usr/local/bin/pi-pbt build-run --provider zai-coding-cn --model glm-5.3 --lang en --build-cmd "cargo check --lib" \
  --scope src/backend/cast.rs \
  --func classify_cast_with_f128
```

title: Bug: invalid float↔pointer casts silently accepted; float→pointer compiled as raw bit reinterpretation
body:
# Bug: invalid float↔pointer casts silently accepted; float→pointer compiled as raw bit reinterpretation

**Law:** C11 6.5.4 (cast operators): a cast between a pointer type and a floating type is a constraint violation — a conforming implementation must emit a diagnostic. Reference: gcc rejects both directions ("error: cannot convert to a pointer type", "pointer value used where a floating-point value was expected"); clang likewise.

**Impact:** ccc silently accepts `(double)ptr` and `(void*)dbl` (both invalid C) and compiles them with invented, asymmetric semantics:

- pointer→float emits a value conversion — but through the **mis-classified signed arm** of issue #4 (`SignedToFloat { from_ty: Ptr }` → bare `fildl` on i686), producing wrong values for pointers ≥ 0x80000000;
- float→pointer emits **no conversion at all**: the raw IEEE-754 bit pattern's low word is used as the pointer value (bit reinterpretation). `(void*)2147483648.0` therefore yields pointer `0x00000000` (low 32 bits of `0x41E0000000000000`), not any value-derived address.

This bug also **shields** the second impact mechanism claimed in issue #4 (float→Ptr on ILP32 selecting `FloatToUnsigned { to_u64: true }` → 8-byte conversion into a 4-byte slot): that classifier defect is real but this frontend behavior intercepts the construct first, so the emitter route never fires from C source.

**Function:** frontend — cast expression lowering for pointer↔floating type combinations (sema/lowering of `Cast` expressions; exact site TBD during fix)

**Detected by:** manual verification of issue #4 (fermat-hkrc/claudes-c-compiler#4).

**Minimal input:**
```c
volatile double d = 2147483648.0;
void *q = (void*)d;          /* invalid C: gcc errors; ccc accepts, q = 0x00000000 (bitcast) */
```
```c
volatile unsigned long u = 0x80000000UL;
void *p = (void*)u;
double x = (double)p;        /* invalid C: gcc errors; ccc converts as SIGNED → -2147483648.0 */
```

**Expected:** a diagnostic for both constructs (constraint violation), like gcc/clang. If ccc deliberately supports these as extensions, the semantics must be defined and documented — and pointer→float must at least be unsigned-correct (issue #4).

**Actual (i686 backend, verified):**

```console
$ gcc probe.c -o /dev/null
error: cannot convert to a pointer type                    # gcc: rejected

$ ccc-i686 -S probe.c -o probe.s && grep -cE "fisttp|cvt" probe.s
0                                                          # no conversion emitted (float->ptr = bitcast)

$ qemu-i386-static probe                                    # runtime check (see issue #4 record)
f2p mismatch: (void*)2147483648.0 != (void*)0x80000000      # q = 0x00000000
```

**Severity:** medium (silent acceptance of invalid code with surprising semantics; no conforming program is affected, but it masks issue #4's second mechanism and produces garbage pointers/NaNs with no diagnostic)

**Regression test:** `/tmp/i4_f2p.c` and `/tmp/i4_syscall.c` from the issue #4 verification record (`pbt-out/verified_bug/issue#4_Ptr_not_treated_as_unsigned_for_float_casts.md`); a minimal regression test is `assert diag((void*)1.5)` once the diagnostic exists.

**Related:** issue #4 (this bug both exposes its pointer→float half and shields its float→Ptr half).

## Found by

Manual verification of [issue #4](https://github.com/fermat-hkrc/claudes-c-compiler/issues/4) during issue triage (original issue #4 found by the PBT campaign below):

```bash
/usr/local/bin/pi-pbt build-run --provider zai-coding-cn --model glm-5.3 --lang en --build-cmd "cargo check --lib" \
  --scope src/backend/cast.rs \
  --func classify_cast_with_f128
```

title: Bug: PUA encoding silently corrupts source files containing literal U+E080..U+E0FF characters (3 bytes -> 1 byte)
body:
**Law:** `bytes_to_string` then lexer-side `decode_pua_byte` must preserve the original bytes of any accepted input (module doc, src/common/encoding.rs:8-10: "encode non-UTF-8 bytes using Unicode Private Use Area (PUA) code points, then decode them back to raw bytes in the lexer").

**Impact:** A valid UTF-8 C source file that legitimately contains a Private Use Area character in the range U+E080..U+E0FF (e.g. inside a string literal — exactly the code points CCC chose for its encoding scheme) is silently corrupted during lexing: the 3-byte UTF-8 sequence decodes back to a single byte 0x80..0xFF. String literal content changes without any diagnostic. Silent data loss on input the API accepts.

**Function:** `ccc::common::encoding::{bytes_to_string, decode_pua_byte}` (src/common/encoding.rs:22, :80)

**Detected by:** Algebraic round-trip property (encode∘decode = identity); property P6 `pua_roundtrip`, proptest 1000 cases (2026-09-15 PBT campaign).

**Minimal input:** byte vector `[0xEE, 0x82, 0x80]` (UTF-8 encoding of U+E080):
1. `bytes_to_string([0xEE,0x82,0x80])` → "\u{E080}" (valid UTF-8 is passed through unchanged)
2. `decode_pua_byte("\u{E080}".as_bytes(), 0)` → returns `(0x80, 3)` (encoding.rs:90-96 matches `EE 82 80` as a PUA-encoded byte)
3. Round-trip result: `[0x80]` — the original 3 bytes are gone

**Expected:** Preserve original bytes, or document/reject the collision class (the scheme cannot distinguish "bytes we PUA-encoded" from "valid UTF-8 that was there all along" without extra state or an escaping mechanism).

**Actual:** Silent 3-bytes→1-byte corruption for any source containing U+E080..U+E0FF.

**Severity:** low (PUA characters in real-world C sources are rare; GCC/Clang never transcode and keep raw bytes)

**Full report:** pbt-out/bug_reports/encoding_pua_collision.md (branch explore/pbt-test)

# Bug: XZR and x31 are accepted as ldNr base (encoded as SP)
**Law:** ARM/gas/llvm-mc accept only Xn|SP as the base. `[xzr]` and `[x31]` are invalid (SP is the Rn=31 spelling).

**Expected:** Err
**Actual:** Ok — parse_reg_num maps xzr and x31 to 31.
**Severity:** medium

title: Bug: LD2R/LD4R S bit encoded at bit 12 instead of bit 21
body:
# Bug: LD2R/LD4R S bit encoded at bit 12 instead of bit 21
**Law:** Valid ld2r/ld4r must match llvm-mc/gas: AdvSIMD replicate encoding places the structure-count S bit at bit 21 (1 for LD2R/LD4R, 0 for LD1R/LD3R) with bit 12 clear.
**Impact:** Every LD2R and LD4R instruction is assembled to the wrong 32-bit word, so objects disagree with gas/llvm-mc and will not execute the intended replicate load.
**Function:** encode_neon_ldnr
**Detected by:** Differential vs llvm-mc / algebraic.invariant (ARM fields)
**Minimal input:** `ld2r {v0.8b, v1.8b}, [x1]` → SUT 0x0d40d020, llvm-mc/gas 0x0d60c020. Also `ld4r {v0.8b, v1.8b, v2.8b, v3.8b}, [x0]` → SUT 0x0d40f000, llvm-mc 0x0d60e000.
**Expected:** bit21=1, bit12=0 for n=2/4 (gas `ld2r {v0.8b, v1.8b}, [x1]` = 0x0d60c020)
**Actual:** bit21=0, bit12=1 (`s_bit << 12` in neon.rs:1569). LD3R happens to match because s_bit=0.
**Severity:** high
**Regression test:** src/backend/arm/assembler/encoder/neon.rs test_encode_neon_ldnr_regression_ld2r_s_bit / test_encode_neon_ldnr_regression_ld4r_s_bit

body:
# Bug: Illegal post-index immediate is accepted
**Law:** gas/llvm-mc require the post-index immediate to equal num_structs*esize (e.g. ld2r .8b → #2). `#0`, `#-1`, `#4` on ld2r .8b are invalid.
**Impact:** Wrong post-index immediates encode as the immediate-post-index form (Rm=11111) regardless of the offset, so the assembler accepts illegal syntax and the writeback size is not checked.
**Function:** encode_neon_ldnr
**Detected by:** Negative/error contract

title: Bug: encode_extr panics or encodes out-of-range #lsb

# Bug: encode_extr panics or encodes out-of-range #lsb
**Law:** EXTR requires 0 <= lsb <= 31 (W) / 63 (X). Out-of-range immediates must be rejected with Err (llvm-mc: immediate must be an integer in range [0, 31] / [0, 63]).
**Impact:** `extr w0, w0, w0, #-1` panics in debug (`attempt to shift left with overflow` at `lsb << 10` after `-1i64 as u32`). Other out-of-range values that do not overflow (e.g. lsb=32 for W) encode an EXTR word with an illegal imms field instead of Err. A panic on assembler input is a crash of the builtin assembler.
**Function:** encode_extr
**Detected by:** Negative/Error Contract (4e)
**Minimal input:** lsb=-1, is_64=false — `extr w0, w0, w0, #-1` (serial reconfirm with --test-threads=1)
**Expected:** Err
**Actual:** panic (debug overflow) rather than Err. Related: lsb=32 for W and lsb=64 for X encode Ok(Word) with imms overlapping neighbouring fields.
**Severity:** high
**Fix:** Reject lsb outside 0..=31 (W) / 0..=63 (X) before shifting into the imms field.
**Regression test:** src/backend/arm/assembler/encoder/bitfield.rs::test_encode_extr_regression_lsb_neg

# Bug: encode_prfm register-offset form uses the wrong opcode bits
**Law:** ARM ARM PRFM (register) is `11 111 0 00 10 1 Rm option S 10 Rn Rt` (base 0xF8A00800). The SUT comment at load_store.rs:764 states the same encoding. llvm-mc emits 0xF8A16800 for `prfm pldl1keep, [x0, x1]`.

# Bug: encode_uxtw emits MOV Wd,Wn (ORR) instead of UBFM Xd,Xn,#0,#31
**Law:** ARM ARM C6 UXTW is the assembler alias of UBFM Xd, Xn, #0, #31 (sf=1 opc=10 N=1 immr=0 imms=31). llvm-mc `-triple=aarch64` encodes `uxtw x0, w1` as `0xD3407C20` (disassembled `ubfx x0, x1, #0, #32`). GNU-style assembler contract: same textual assembly as gas, same 32-bit word.
**Impact:** Every `uxtw` instruction is assembled as 32-bit `ORR Wd, WZR, Wn` (`MOV Wd, Wn`). Object files disagree with gas/llvm-mc; disassembly shows `mov w0, w1` instead of `ubfx x0, x1, #0, #32`. Semantically similar for the register file but a wrong encoding for an assembler.
**Function:** encode_uxtw
**Detected by:** Differential vs llvm-mc; Algebraic — Metamorphic (UBFM #0,#31 alias); Algebraic — Invariant (ARM fields)
**Minimal input:** `[Reg("x0"), Reg("w1")]` (uxtw x0, w1); also shrunk `[Reg("x0"), Reg("w0")]` (rd=0, rn=0)
**Expected:** `Ok(Word(0xD3407C20))` for x0, w1; `Ok(Word(0xD3407C00))` for x0, w0
**Actual:** `Ok(Word(0x2A0103E0))` for x0, w1 (`mov w0, w1`); `Ok(Word(0x2A0003E0))` for x0, w0. Formula used: `(0b001010100 << 23) | (rn << 16) | (0b11111 << 5) | rd` (32-bit ORR with Rn=WZR, Rm=Wn).
**Severity:** high
**Regression test:** src/backend/arm/assembler/encoder/data_processing.rs `test_encode_uxtw_regression_mov_not_ubfm`
**Serial reconfirm:** reproduced with `PBT_TEST_JOBS=1 cargo test --lib encode_uxtw -- --test-threads=1`

title: Bug: encode_shift accepts size-mismatched and non-GP destinations
body:
# Bug: encode_shift accepts size-mismatched and non-GP destinations
**Law:** A shift/rotate destination must be a general-purpose register (or memory) whose width matches the mnemonic suffix. llvm-mc and Intel SDM Group 2 reject `shlw %al` and `shlq %xmm0`.
**Impact:** Public AT&T text such as `shlw $1, %al` and `shlq $1, %xmm0` is accepted and encoded as a different instruction (`shlw %ax` and `shlq %rax`), because `reg_num` maps `al`/`xmm0` to encoding 0. Silent wrong machine code.
**Function:** encode_shift
**Detected by:** Negative/Error Contract (4e) — llvm-mc/Intel SDM reject; README claims AT&T/GAS compatibility
**Minimal input:**
- `shlw $1, %al` (mnemonic=shlw, shift_op=4, ops=[Imm(1), Reg(al)])
- `shlq $1, %xmm0` (mnemonic=shlq, shift_op=4, ops=[Imm(1), Reg(xmm0)])
**Expected:** Err
**Actual:**
- `shlw $1, %al` → Ok([0x66, 0xd1, 0xe0]) which is `shlw %ax`
- `shlq $1, %xmm0` → Ok([0x48, 0xd1, 0xe0]) which is `shlq %rax`
**Severity:** high
**Regression test:** src/backend/x86/assembler/encoder/gp_integer.rs `test_encode_shift_regression_mixed_size_shlw_al` and `test_encode_shift_regression_non_gp_xmm0`
**Serial reconfirm:** PBT_TEST_JOBS=1 RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 reproduced `shlw`/`al`; the xmm0 case is a deterministic regression.
**Root cause:** encode_shift uses `mnemonic_size_suffix` for opcode width and `reg_num` for ModR/M, with no check that the destination is a GP register of that width. `reg_num` aliases xmm/ymm/mm/st/segment names onto GP encodings.

**Impact:** `negs wsp, w0` is accepted and encoded as `negs wzr, w0`. llvm-mc/gas reject SP as a NEGS operand.
**Function:** encode_negs
**Detected by:** Negative/Error Contract (4e)
**Minimal input:** `[Reg("wsp"), Reg("w0")]` (which=0, is_64=false, other=0)
**Expected:** Err
**Actual:** Ok(Word) with Rd=31 (WZR)
**Severity:** medium
**Regression test:** src/backend/arm/assembler/encoder/data_processing.rs::test_encode_negs_regression_sp

# Bug: encode_neg silently ignores extra operands
**Law:** RISC-V `neg` is a two-operand pseudoinstruction (`neg rd, rs`). `encode_neg([rd, rs, extra])` must return Err, matching llvm-mc which rejects `neg rd, rs, extra`.
**Impact:** Source text `neg zero, zero, zero` is assembled as `neg zero, zero` (`sub x0, x0, x0`) instead of being rejected. The assembled object silently disagrees with the written instruction.
**Function:** encode_neg
**Detected by:** Algebraic — Negative/Error Contract (4e)
**Minimal input:** operands = [Reg("zero"), Reg("zero"), Reg("zero")]
**Expected:** Err (invalid operand; documented form is `neg rd, rs`; llvm-mc: "invalid operand for instruction")
**Actual:** Ok(Word(0x40000033)) — extra operand ignored; encodes as `neg zero, zero`
**Severity:** medium

title: Bug: encode_neon_shift_right truncates i64 shift via `as u32`

# Bug: encode_neon_shift_right truncates i64 shift via `as u32`
**Law:** The shift immediate is an i64 (`Operand::Imm`). Values outside [1, esize] must be rejected; the encoder must not fold the immediate modulo 2^32.
**Impact:** `Imm(1 + 2^32)` encodes as `#1`, so an out-of-range shift is silently accepted as a different in-range shift.
**Function:** encode_neon_shift_right
**Detected by:** Negative/Error Contract (4e) — encode_neon_shift_right_neg_shift_i64_trunc
**Minimal input:** `encode_neon_shift_right([v0.8b, v0.8b, Imm(4294967297)], u=0, opcode=0b001001)`
**Expected:** `Err` (4294967297 ∉ [1, 8])
**Actual:** `Ok(EncodeResult::Word(_))` encoding the same word as `#1` — `let shift = get_imm(...) as u32` (`neon.rs:1459`)
**Severity:** medium

title: Bug: x86 encoder does not validate register size against mnemonic suffix (16-bit name silently encoded as its 64/32-bit twin)
body:
# Bug: x86 encoder does not validate register size against mnemonic suffix (16-bit name silently encoded as its 64/32-bit twin)

**Law:** The mnemonic size suffix (`q/l/w/b`) fixes the operand size; using a general-purpose register name of the wrong size (e.g. 16-bit `%sp` with `movq`) is invalid AT&T assembly that GNU as rejects (`Error: operand type mismatch`). The encoder must reject it — it must never silently encode `%sp` as `%rsp`.

**Impact:** `assemble()` is a public entry point (assembler/mod.rs:15) and is also used for hand-written `.s` files. Accepting invalid input and emitting semantically wrong machine code (a 16-bit intent encoded as a 64-bit instruction) is a silent wrong result: a user writing `movq %sp, %rax` expects a diagnostic but gets `mov %rsp,%rax`. The compiler's own codegen only emits size-consistent operands, so the internal path is unaffected — but for any hand-written / external input this is silent semantic corruption.

**Function:** `src/backend/x86/assembler/encoder/` (registers.rs `reg_num` is size-agnostic; `encode_mov_rr` / `encode_alu` / etc. in gp_integer.rs never check the size family of `Register.name`)

**Detected by:** negative/error-contract property `prop_malformed_rejected` (encoder_pbt.rs); the differential properties independently flagged the same input class as SUT-Ok/gas-Err.

**Minimal input:**
| Text | GNU as | SUT output | Actual semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| `movq %sp, %rax` | rejected | `48 89 e0` | `mov %rsp,%rax` |
| `movl %bx, %eax` | rejected | `89 d8` | `mov %ebx,%eax` |
| `addw %eax, %bx` | rejected | `66 01 c3` | `add %eax,%ebx` |
| `movq %ax, %rdi` | rejected | `48 89 c7` | `mov %rax,%rdi` |

**Expected:** `Err` (size mismatch), like GNU as's "operand type mismatch".
**Actual:** `Ok(bytes)` — the same-family register number is reused (registers.rs:4-21 `reg_num` maps "sp"/"rsp"/"esp" all to 5); size information is lost along the encoding path.

**Severity:** medium (silent wrong encoding on a public assembler entry; internal codegen path unaffected)

**Regression test:** `src/backend/x86/assembler/encoder/encoder_pbt.rs::witness_register_size_mismatch` (`#[ignore]`d witness; un-ignore after the fix — it asserts the inputs above return `is_err` and should then turn green)

# Bug: encode_ldur_stur silently wraps offsets outside signed 9-bit range
**Law:** ARM ARM unscaled/unprivileged load/store immediate is a signed 9-bit byte offset in [-256, 255]. llvm-mc rejects `#256` and `#-257` (`index must be an integer in range [-256, 255]`). encode_ldur_stur must Err outside that range.

# Bug: encode_neon_sli does not reject out-of-range shift
**Law:** Vector SLI shift must be an integer in [0, esize(T)-1] (8B/16B: 0..7, 4H/8H: 0..15, 2S/4S: 0..31, 2D: 0..63). Values outside that range must be rejected with Err, matching llvm-mc `immediate must be an integer in range [0, esize-1]`.
**Impact:** Negative immediates panic in debug (`attempt to add with overflow` on `esize + shift`) and wrap in release, encoding a different legal shift. `shift == esize` is masked (`(esize + shift) & mask`) into reserved immh=0000, producing an undefined encoding that gas/llvm-mc reject.
**Function:** encode_neon_sli
**Detected by:** Negative/Error Contract (4e)
**Minimal input:**
- rd=0, rn=0, t="8b", shift=-1 — `sli v0.8b, v0.8b, #-1` panics in debug (`8 + ( -1 as u32 )` overflows)
- rd=0, rn=0, t="8b", shift=8 — `sli v0.8b, v0.8b, #8` returns Ok with immh:immb = (8+8)&0xF = 0 (reserved)
**Expected:** Err
**Actual:** debug panic on shift < 0; Ok(Word) with wrapped/masked immh:immb on shift >= esize
**Severity:** high
**Regression test:** src/backend/arm/assembler/encoder/neon.rs::encode_neon_sli_pbt::test_encode_neon_sli_regression_negative_shift and test_encode_neon_sli_regression_shift_eq_esize

title: Bug: encode_eon rejects the GNU EON-immediate alias
body:
# Bug: encode_eon rejects the GNU EON-immediate alias
**Law:** Gas/llvm-mc accept `eon Rd, Rn, #imm` as an alias of `eor Rd, Rn, #~imm` when ~imm is a valid AArch64 bitmask. The built-in assembler claims gas-compatible textual assembly (README.md:5-14) and dispatches every `eon` mnemonic to encode_eon.
**Impact:** Valid GNU assembly such as `eon w0, w0, #0xaaaaaaaa` (llvm-mc: `eor w0, w0, #0x55555555`, encoding 0x5200f000) fails to assemble. Sibling `encode_bic` already implements the corresponding AND #~imm alias; EON is missing the EOR counterpart.
**Function:** encode_eon
**Detected by:** Differential — llvm-mc AArch64 assembler
**Minimal input:** `eon w0, w0, #0xaaaaaaaa` (rd=0, rn=0, is_64=false, seed=0)
**Expected:** Ok(Word(0x5200f000)) matching llvm-mc `eor w0, w0, #0x55555555`
**Actual:** Err("expected register at operand 2, got Some(Imm(2863311530))") — get_reg is applied to operand 2 with no Imm path.
**Severity:** medium

**Impact:** A third operand (`cbz x0, labl0, x1`) is silently dropped and a CondBr19 reloc is still emitted. That hides parse/typo errors and diverges from gas/llvm-mc, which reject the instruction.

**Actual:** Ok(WordWithReloc { word: 0xb4000000, reloc: CondBr19, symbol: "labl0", addend: 0 }) — get_reg/get_symbol only inspect operands 0 and 1.
**Severity:** medium
**Regression test:** src/backend/arm/assembler/encoder/compare_branch.rs `test_encode_cbz_regression_extra_operand`

# Bug: encode_branch rejects immediate PC-offset form `b #imm`
**Law:** For every 4-byte-aligned offset in the ARM ARM B range [-2^27, 2^27-4], encode_branch([Imm(imm)]) must equal Word(llvm-mc("b #imm")).
**Impact:** GNU-style assembly that uses an explicit PC offset (`b #0`, `b #4`, `b #-134217728`) fails to assemble. title: Bug: Ptr is not treated as U64/U32 for float and F128 casts
body:
# Bug: Ptr is not treated as U64/U32 for float and F128 casts
**Law:** Ptr normalization happens before classification: Ptr is equivalent to U64 on LP64 and U32 on ILP32, so pointer-to-float must be unsigned and float-to-pointer on ILP32 must use the 32-bit unsigned path.
**Impact:** Pointer-to-float/F128 is classified as signed. On i686, `emit_signed_to_f64` / `emit_signed_to_f128` then use `fildl` without the unsigned high-bit correction, so addresses with the high bit set convert to negative floating values. Float-to-pointer on ILP32 is classified as `FloatToUnsigned { to_u64: true }`; i686 matches that arm with `emit_f32_to_i64` and stores an 8-byte conversion into a 4-byte pointer slot.
**Function:** classify_cast_with_f128
**Detected by:** Algebraic — Metamorphic (4c) and Algebraic — Invariant (4d)
**Minimal input:**
- `classify_cast_with_f128(Ptr, F32, false)` with `target_ptr_size=4` → `SignedToFloat { to_f64: false, from_ty: Ptr }`
- `classify_cast_with_f128(Ptr, F128, true)` with `target_ptr_size=4` → `SignedToF128 { from_ty: Ptr }`
- `classify_cast_with_f128(F32, Ptr, false)` with `target_ptr_size=4` → `FloatToUnsigned { from_f64: false, to_u64: true }`
**Expected:**
- Ptr → F32 equals U32 → F32: `UnsignedToFloat { to_f64: false, from_ty: U32 }`
- Ptr → F128 native equals U32 → F128: `UnsignedToF128 { from_ty: U32 }`
- F32 → Ptr on ILP32 equals F32 → U32: `FloatToUnsigned { from_f64: false, to_u64: false }`
**Actual:** Ptr source is classified as signed; Ptr dest forces `to_u64: true` regardless of pointer width. Root cause: F128 handling and the float-to-int / int-to-float arms run before (and skip) the Ptr-normalization block, which is gated on `!from_ty.is_float() && !to_ty.is_float()`.
**Severity:** high
**Regression test:** src/backend/cast.rs (`test_classify_cast_with_f128_regression_ptr_to_f32_unsigned`, `test_classify_cast_with_f128_regression_ptr_to_f128_unsigned`, `test_classify_cast_with_f128_regression_f32_to_ptr_ilp32`)
**Serial reconfirmation:** reproduced with `PBT_TEST_JOBS=1` / `--test-threads=1` (same shrunk witnesses).

# Bug: float-to-unsigned casts store U8/U16 as signed I8/I16, so to_i64() sign-extends
**Law:** Unsigned sub-64-bit IR constants must be stored as I64 with a zero-extended value so `to_i64()` does not sign-extend (e.g. U8 128 → 128, not -128). Documented on `IrConst::from_i64` and this function's own docstring (`200.0 as u8 = 200`). Same-job float-to-int folding in `constant_fold` uses `from_i64`.
**Impact:** Compile-time `(unsigned char)128.0` / `(unsigned short)40000.0` folded via `cast_float_to_target` (simplify, const_eval, coerce_to) become negative `to_i64()` values. Subsequent integer promotion, comparisons, and GVN hashing disagree with the `constant_fold` path, which stores `I64(128)`.
**Function:** IrConst::cast_float_to_target
**Detected by:** Differential vs from_i64; Algebraic invariant (to_i64 zero-extend)
**Minimal input:** `cast_float_to_target(128.0, IrType::U8)` — `to_i64()` yields `Some(-128)`. Also `cast_float_to_target(0.0, IrType::U8) = I8(0)` vs `from_i64(0, U8) = I64(0)`.
**Expected:** `Some(IrConst::I64(128))` (and `to_i64() == Some(128)`), matching `from_i64(128, IrType::U8)`. Docstring example: `200.0 as u8 = 200`.
**Actual:** `Some(IrConst::I8(-128))`; `to_i64() == Some(-128)`. U16 is the same class (`I16` instead of `I64`). U32 already uses I64 and is consistent.
**Severity:** medium
**Regression test:** src/ir/constants.rs::cast_float_to_target_pbt::test_cast_float_to_target_regression_u8_high_bit
**Serial reconfirmation:** reproduced with `PBT_TEST_JOBS=1 cargo test --lib cast_float_to_target_unsigned_to_i64 -- --test-threads=1`

## Found by

```bash
/home/toan/github/pbt-agent/dist/pi-pbt build-run --provider xai --model grok-4.6 --lang en --build-cmd "cargo check --lib" \
  --scope src/ir/constants.rs \
  --func IrConst::cast_float_to_target
```

title: Bug: cast_float_to_target panics on f64 subnormals when targeting F128
body:
# Bug: cast_float_to_target panics on f64 subnormals when targeting F128
**Law:** ∀ fv ∈ f64. `cast_float_to_target(fv, IrType::F128)` returns `Some(LongDouble(fv, bytes))` without panicking. The F128 arm is `IrConst::long_double(fv)`, whose f64 approximation field is `fv` (`src/ir/constants.rs:167-168, 279`). Subnormals are valid f64 values; the API does not exclude them.
**Impact:** Any compile-time cast of a subnormal `double` to `long double` (or coerce-to F128) panics the compiler in debug builds (`attempt to subtract with overflow`). In overflow-unchecked builds the same `u128` subtraction wraps and emits garbage binary128 bytes.
**Function:** IrConst::cast_float_to_target
**Detected by:** Algebraic invariant (F128 approximation field)
**Minimal input:** `bits = 9223372036854775809` (`0x8000000000000001`) — negative f64 subnormal (sign=1, biased_exp=0, mantissa=1). Any subnormal (e.g. bits=1) hits the same path.
**Expected:** `Some(IrConst::LongDouble(fv, bytes))` with `fv.to_bits() == 0x8000000000000001`, no panic.
**Actual:** panic at `src/common/long_double.rs:1040` in `f64_to_f128_bytes_lossless`: `(d.biased_exp as u128 - 1023 + 16383)` underflows because subnormals have `biased_exp == 0` and are not classified as zero (`mantissa != 0`) or special.
**Severity:** high
**Regression test:** src/ir/constants.rs::cast_float_to_target_pbt::test_cast_float_to_target_regression_f128_neg_subnormal
**Serial reconfirmation:** reproduced with `PBT_TEST_JOBS=1 cargo test --lib cast_float_to_target_f128 -- --test-threads=1`

## Found by

```bash
/home/toan/github/pbt-agent/dist/pi-pbt build-run --provider xai --model grok-4.6 --lang en --build-cmd "cargo check --lib" \
  --scope src/ir/constants.rs \
  --func IrConst::cast_float_to_target
```
